questions.q: While reviewing a status report, a project manager notices that, over a period of six months, the coding quality for one developer is statistically lower than another developer assigned the same task. Which tool should the project manager use to trace the problem's source back to its actionable root cause? *

o.t: Histogram
Control chart
Scatter diagram
Ishikawa diagram

questions.e: The correct answer is: D. Ishikawa diagram An Ishikawa diagram, also known as a fishbone or cause-and-effect diagram, helps identify and trace the root cause of a problem by categorizing potential causes in a structured manner. This tool is useful in identifying the actionable root cause of lower coding quality.

questions.q: A project has been closed and customer care needs to measure customer satisfaction with the deliverables. What should be done next? *

o.t: Negotiate additional contract with customer for similar service.
Schedule meeting with stakeholders and customer to discuss lessons learned.
Evaluate project deliverables and review customer feedback documents.
Audit project success by reviewing closing documentation for each project phase.

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Evaluate project deliverables and review customer feedback documents. After a project has been closed, the next step in measuring customer satisfaction with the deliverables is to evaluate the deliverables and review customer feedback. This ensures that the project met customer expectations and allows for understanding their satisfaction level.

questions.q: A project manager discovers a significant flaw in a major project deliverable. Which project management process is being performed? *

o.t: Manage Quality
Control Quality
Plan Quality Management
Statistical Sampling

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. Control Quality The Control Quality process involves monitoring and evaluating project deliverables to ensure that they meet the required quality standards. Discovering a significant flaw in a major project deliverable falls under this process, as it is concerned with identifying defects and ensuring the deliverables conform to the project’s quality requirements.

questions.q: A project manager assigned to an existing project finds that the deliverable quality has been inconsistent. The project manager finds that the team is not adhering to the development standards. What practice should the project manager employ to ensure higher quality? *

o.t: Perform a full inspection since there is no margin for error.
Introduce sampling as a cost-effective and time-efficient way to ensure quality.
Implement a continuous improvement process to ensure consistent outcomes.
Add a unit of work for a specific period of time to prove the solution is viable.

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Implement a continuous improvement process to ensure consistent outcomes. Introducing a continuous improvement process, such as Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), helps ensure that quality standards are consistently met by regularly assessing and improving processes. This approach allows for long-term quality enhancement and consistency in deliverables.

questions.q: T he first version delivered to the quality control team has poor performance, and the testers are complaining that they cannot complete all the test cases as planned. Which is a tool to help to monitor performance? *

o.t: Run Chart
Data Flow Diagram
Flow Chart
Non-Control Chart

questions.e: The correct answer is: A. Run Chart A Run Chart is a tool that helps monitor performance over time. It plots data points in sequence and allows the project manager to identify trends, patterns, or variations in performance, which can help in addressing issues like poor performance in a deliverable.

questions.q: During a periodic review with stakeholders, the project sponsor asks how the project will measure satisfactory completion of the deliverables and how those measurements are applied. Where can the project manager find this information? *

o.t: Scope management plan.
Requirements management plan.
Quality management plan.
Work performance reports.

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Quality management plan. The Quality Management Plan contains the information regarding how the project will measure satisfactory completion of the deliverables, including the quality metrics, standards, and procedures for ensuring that deliverables meet the required criteria.

questions.q: A project manager is reviewing work performance data in preparation for the Close Project process. The data reveals that one of the deliverables was not accepted. The estimated work required to complete acceptance of the deliverable will delay the project completion date by two months. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Allocate the contingency reserve to procure resources needed for completion.
Update the schedule and perform the work.
Issue a change request for review by the change control board (CCB).
Update the watch list in the risk register.

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Issue a change request for review by the change control board (CCB). Since the project completion date will be delayed due to the need to complete the deliverable, the project manager should issue a change request. This request will go through the Change Control Board (CCB) for review and approval before any adjustments to the schedule or resources are made. This ensures that changes are properly evaluated and controlled.

questions.q: A company is using Lean Six Sigma methodology on a project. Midway through the project, an external Lean consultant is invited to conduct an audit to ensure that the methodology is being properly applied. Which process is being employed? *

o.t: Manage Quality
Control Quality
Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis
Plan Quality Management

questions.e: The correct answer is: A. Manage Quality The Manage Quality process focuses on ensuring that the project's quality standards are properly implemented and continuously improved. Inviting a Lean consultant to conduct an audit to verify that the Lean Six Sigma methodology is being properly applied is an example of the Manage Quality process.

questions.q: Quality management is a vital aspect of any project. Which of the following quality control aspects is a component of a high functioning measurement system? *

o.t: Accuracy
Non-precision
Non-repeatability
Duration

questions.e: The correct answer is: A. Accuracy In a high-functioning measurement system, accuracy is a critical component. It refers to how close the measured value is to the true or accepted value. High accuracy ensures reliable quality control and consistent performance in project deliverables.

questions.q: An application developer took a story card to work that read "Customer can pay using credit card". After the implementation, the functionality was rejected because the application could not accept foreign credit cards. What should the project manager have done to avoid this issue? *

o.t: Described the user story in more detail.
Scheduled the user story for the next iteration.
Performed iterative backlog grooming with the team.
Gathered more detailed requirement specifications from end users.

questions.e: Option A: Described the user story in more detail. Describing a user story in more detail involves adding specific information and acceptance criteria to ensure that all requirements are clearly understood by the development team. This includes: Detailed Requirements: Specifying what needs to be implemented, such as allowing the application to accept both domestic and foreign credit cards. Acceptance Criteria: Defining how to verify that the user story meets the requirements, such as successful payment transactions with various credit card types. Edge Cases: Identifying any special conditions or exceptions, such as handling different currencies or validating international credit card formats. By providing a detailed description, you reduce the risk of incomplete or misunderstood requirements, which helps avoid issues like the one where foreign credit cards were not accepted. However, while this approach addresses immediate clarity, iterative backlog grooming (Option C) ensures that user stories are continuously refined and updated throughout the project, making it a more proactive and ongoing solution.

questions.q: During the development of a project, the project manager noticed that results are not as good as expected. Which tool or document shows which elements are impacting the key metrics? *

o.t: Pareto chart
Run chart
Project charter
Risk register

questions.e: The correct answer is: A. Pareto chart A Pareto chart helps identify and prioritize the most significant factors impacting key metrics by displaying data in descending order of frequency or impact. This tool is useful for determining which elements are contributing the most to the observed issues, allowing the project manager to focus on addressing the most critical factors.

questions.q: A project manager needs to formally complete a project, but a supplier says an invoice has been paid twice. The project manager knows that the invoice was approved, but cannot find evidence of a duplicate payment. The project manager needs to close out this project in order to start a new project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Inform the supplier that payment was made only once, begin the close project process, and begin work on the new project.
Postpone project closure until the accounts payable department can document that the invoice was paid correctly.
Complete all final project documents, delay work on the new project, and update the documents after payment is verified.
Meet with the sponsor of the existing project to obtain approval to begin the new project before the existing project is closed.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. Postpone project closure until the accounts payable department can document that the invoice was paid correctly. Before formally closing the project, it's important to ensure that all financial aspects, including invoice payments, are accurately documented and resolved. Postponing project closure until the accounts payable department can confirm the payment status will help avoid any potential discrepancies or issues that could affect the project's finalization. This ensures that all financial matters are settled properly before moving on to new projects.

questions.q: A pilot project is ready to close and the project team wants to capture the challenges that were overcome and the opportunities for future work. Where will they document this information? *

o.t: Organizational process assets updates
Work performance report
Project management plan
Lessons learned register

questions.e: The correct answer is: D. Lessons learned register The Lessons Learned Register is the appropriate place to document challenges that were overcome and opportunities for future work. This document captures valuable insights and experiences from the project, which can be used to improve future projects and processes.

questions.q: Upon completion of a long-term contract, the project manager confirms with the release manager that all planned features are functioning properly as verified by the quality assurance team. The project manager informs the same to the customer and project stakeholders and obtains the approval to close the project. The project is now closed. For ensuring that the knowledge gained during this project remains available for future reference, what should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Update the lessons learned knowledge base.
Update the risk register before informing project team members.
Update and archive the final procurement file.
Close out the seller performance evaluation documentation.

questions.e: The correct answer is: A. Update the lessons learned knowledge base. To ensure that the knowledge gained during the project remains available for future reference, the project manager should update the lessons learned knowledge base. This documentation captures insights, challenges, and best practices from the project, providing valuable information for future projects and helping to improve organizational processes.

questions.q: A project manager has been selected to deliver one of an organization's key flagship solutions. Critical success factors include agility, market adaptation, and a quick response to market offerings. What is one of the key activities that the project manager should undertake to ensure company success? *

o.t: Review the project objectives with the project sponsor to agree on more realistic and achievable project plans and deliverables.
Request more funding from the project sponsor to hire additional skilled resources and to incorporate additional quality in the project delivery approach and outcome.
Conduct periodical reviews of the project plans, objectives, and deliverables to ensure all relevant data are captured to continue making informed project decisions.
Create a business case after performing a market review, and then submit it to the sponsor to modify the project deliverable to meet the newly defined objectives.

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Conduct periodical reviews of the project plans, objectives, and deliverables to ensure all relevant data are captured to continue making informed project decisions. Conducting periodical reviews allows the project manager to stay aligned with the critical success factors of agility, market adaptation, and quick response. Regularly assessing the project plans, objectives, and deliverables helps ensure that the project can adapt to changes and make informed decisions based on the most current data. This practice supports maintaining the project's alignment with market needs and organizational goals.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a large business transformation project. All of the build deliverables were signed off and the project manager is managing the transition to BAU (Business as Usual). Which of the following are important operational readiness considerations that the project manager needs to consider? (Choose 2). *

o.t: A cheat sheet for core functionality is provided and self training is encouraged.
Formal training and access to documentation should be provided to all users.
Responsibility and accountability are formally handed over to operational teams.
The project team remains responsible for operational support during BAU.

questions.e: The two important operational readiness considerations are: B. Formal training and access to documentation should be provided to all users. C. Responsibility and accountability are formally handed over to operational teams. These considerations ensure that users are properly trained and have access to necessary documentation, and that the operational teams are clearly assigned responsibility and accountability for maintaining and supporting the deliverables in the Business as Usual (BAU) phase.

questions.q: A project manager is formally closing a project that has been completed. Why should the project manager document final project activities? *

o.t: To record case studies and customer references
To log final project performance metrics and quality analysis
To provide lessons learned and archive historical information
To allow the customer to submit invoices and get a receipt of final payment

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. To provide lessons learned and archive historical information Documenting final project activities is crucial for capturing lessons learned and archiving historical information. This documentation helps in understanding what worked well and what didn’t, providing valuable insights for future projects and ensuring that knowledge is preserved for organizational learning and improvement.

questions.q: Which of the following is performed in project/phase closure? *

o.t: Schedule and conduct a project kickoff meeting.
Schedule and conduct a lessons learned meeting.
Schedule and conduct a change control meeting.
Schedule and conduct a project status meeting.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. Schedule and conduct a lessons learned meeting. In project or phase closure, a lessons learned meeting is scheduled and conducted to review and document insights gained throughout the project. This meeting helps capture what went well, what could be improved, and provides valuable information for future projects.

questions.q: A project to develop a new product is nearing its closing phase after 6 months of contributions from the project team and vendor. The project manager has confirmed that the project satisfied the strategic goal it was meant to achieve and received formal documented acceptance from the client and sponsor. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review all contracts with the project team and suppliers.
Disband the project team and return resources to their functional location.
Ensure customer care teams have the training to perform their role.
Document lessons learned for future reference.

questions.q: A large infrastructure organization is reviewing and standardizing project tools and techniques. Regarding the question “When should the decision be made to take corrective action?”, which process group can this question come from? *

o.t: Initiating Process Group
Planning Process Group
Executing Process Group
Monitoring and Controlling Process Group

questions.e: The correct answer is: D. Monitoring and Controlling Process Group Decisions about when to take corrective action are part of the Monitoring and Controlling Process Group. This process group involves tracking project performance, identifying variances from the plan, and implementing corrective actions to ensure that the project remains on track and meets its objectives.

questions.q: The first iteration of an agile project consists of a minimum viable product (MVP) that is now successfully completed. The team members are eager to hand the product over to the customer. How should the product be confirmed as ready for customer use? *

o.t: The scrum master determines that all requirements are satisfied.
The project team agrees the MVP meets the definition of done (DoD).
The senior manager and customer approve and accept the product.
The product owner decides that the MVP passes all required quality tests.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. The project team agrees the MVP meets the definition of done (DoD). In Agile projects, the Definition of Done (DoD) is a critical criterion that determines when a product increment, such as an MVP (Minimum Viable Product), is considered complete and ready for delivery. The project team must agree that the MVP meets the DoD, which includes all agreed-upon requirements and quality standards, before handing it over to the customer. This ensures that the product is fully developed and meets the necessary criteria for customer use.

questions.q: A project manager just completed a project in an organization that values lessons learned. Leadership encourages all the project stakeholders to use the process, tools, and results from the lessons learned repository in future projects. Preparing to update the lessons learned repository, the project manager has gathered relevant project data and feedback. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Store all the comments and recommendations received for future reference.
Analyze and organize the findings with the stakeholders to extract insights.
Document and share the findings with the stakeholders for review and feedback.
Retrieve all of the comments and recommendations received in the past.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. Analyze and organize the findings with the stakeholders to extract insights. Before updating the lessons learned repository, the project manager should analyze and organize the findings with stakeholders to extract actionable insights. This step ensures that the lessons learned are meaningful and provide valuable information for improving future projects. After analysis, the findings can be documented and shared for review and feedback.

questions.q: Which of the following is not considered during project/phase closure? *

o.t: Team celebration ideas
Critical Success Factors
Fast-tracking
Knowledge transfer

questions.e: The correct answer is: C. Fast-tracking Fast-tracking is a technique used during project execution to shorten the project schedule by overlapping phases or activities. It is not a consideration during project or phase closure. In contrast, team celebration ideas, critical success factors, and knowledge transfer are relevant to project closure as they involve recognizing achievements, reviewing success criteria, and ensuring that knowledge is passed on for future use.

questions.q: A project was cancelled during its initiation phase due to lack of adequate resources. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Inform all team members according to guidelines in the communications management plan.
Refer to the company's project closure guidelines.
Perform a risk analysis to determine the impact of terminating the project.
Reassign all resources and reallocate budget.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. Refer to the company's project closure guidelines. When a project is cancelled, even during the initiation phase, the project manager should follow the company's project closure guidelines. These guidelines will provide a structured approach for formally closing out the project, including tasks such as documenting the closure, communicating with stakeholders, and addressing any administrative and contractual obligations.

questions.q: An approved change request adds an incentive to a lump sum contract if the contractor is able to maintain the current baseline schedule. What should now be updated? *

o.t: Scope baseline
Project management plan
Cost baseline
Schedule baseline

questions.e: C. Cost baseline The Cost Baseline represents the approved version of the project budget, including all planned costs, and is used to measure and control project performance. It includes the total estimated costs for the project and is typically established during the planning phase. In the context of the given scenario, where an incentive is added to a lump sum contract for maintaining the current baseline schedule, the following considerations apply: Incentive Impact: The addition of an incentive might affect the cost baseline by increasing the total project cost. Therefore, the cost baseline should be updated to reflect the new financial terms and ensure accurate tracking and reporting of project costs. Integration with Project Management Plan: While the cost baseline is a critical component, the overall Project Management Plan would need to be updated to integrate the changes brought about by the incentive and ensure all aspects of the project are aligned. So, although the cost baseline is affected, it is part of the larger Project Management Plan, which encompasses all updates and changes related to project execution.

questions.q: A project manager is reviewing project histories, resources, and performance data to apply stored knowledge to a new project. Where is the first place the project manager should look? *

o.t: Previously accepted project charters.
PMIS system.
Quality management tools.
Baseline versus actual performance reports.

questions.e: The correct answer is: B. PMIS system. The Project Management Information System (PMIS) is typically the first place a project manager should look when reviewing project histories, resources, and performance data. The PMIS contains a repository of historical data, including past project performance, resource utilization, and lessons learned, which can be applied to new projects. It provides comprehensive and centralized information that helps in making informed decisions and applying best practices from previous projects.

questions.q: As a project manager of a technology firm, a change in the scope is required to implement a change in the project. What tools can be utilized to better understand the impact of the change? *

o.t: Pareto chart
Fishbone diagram
Deming's PDCA cycle
Cause and effect diagram

questions.e: C. Deming's PDCA Cycle Deming's PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) Cycle is a continuous improvement methodology used to manage and improve processes. It involves four key steps: Plan: Identify and analyze the problem or change requirement, and develop a plan for addressing it. Do: Implement the plan on a small scale to test its effectiveness. Check: Monitor and evaluate the results of the implementation to see if it meets the objectives and solves the problem. Act: Based on the evaluation, take action to standardize the successful changes or refine the plan if needed. While the PDCA cycle is excellent for process improvement and implementing changes in a controlled manner, it is not specifically focused on understanding the impact of scope changes. It is more about managing and improving processes over time rather than directly analyzing the impact of a change. For understanding the impact of a scope change in a project, tools like the Cause and Effect Diagram or other impact assessment tools are more directly applicable, as they help visualize and assess how the change will affect various aspects of the project.

questions.q: A group of stakeholders at a financial institution are conducting a project closure review. Some of the stakeholders are concerned that the project deliverables do not satisfy the established closure criteria. What is the first thing that the project manager should do to address this issue? *

o.t: Assure the stakeholders that the project deliverables satisfy all established closure criteria.
Propose that the closure criteria be amended by removing the criteria that have not been met.
Take corrective measures by adapting the closure criteria and extending the project timeline.
Perform a thorough analysis to determine why the closure criteria have not been satisfied.

questions.e: The correct answer is: D. Perform a thorough analysis to determine why the closure criteria have not been satisfied. Before taking any further action, the project manager should first perform a thorough analysis to understand why the project deliverables are perceived as not meeting the established closure criteria. This involves reviewing the project requirements, deliverables, and any gaps or issues identified by the stakeholders. Once the reasons are understood, the project manager can then address the issues appropriately, which might involve corrective actions, discussions with stakeholders, or adjustments to the project closure process.

questions.q: A project steering group has made a decision to change the vendor that will deliver a component of a project. Which of the following activities should be included in the handover? (Choose 2). *

o.t: The old vendor should provide training for the new one and assist with the transition.
Both vendors should provide additional incentives for staff during the transition.
The new vendor should take over activities as per the existing project plan.
The new vendor should shadow the old vendor to ensure knowledge transfer.

questions.e: The correct answers are: A. The old vendor should provide training for the new one and assist with the transition. D. The new vendor should shadow the old vendor to ensure knowledge transfer. These activities are important for a smooth transition between vendors. Training and knowledge transfer are critical to ensure that the new vendor can effectively take over responsibilities and maintain continuity in the project's progress.

questions.q: You are the project manager on a project delivered by a Scrum team. The project sponsors are not familiar with the Scrum framework and were invited to attend the first release retrospective. They ask you to describe the scope of this event. Which of the following are the goals of the retrospective event? (Choose 3) *

o.t: Identify what is working well and define actions to reinforce them.
Identify what is not working and define actions to rectify them.
Identify top improvement areas and define actions to implement them.
Identify unfinished deliverables and define actions to complete them.

questions.e: The correct answers are: A. Identify what is working well and define actions to reinforce them. B. Identify what is not working and define actions to rectify them. C. Identify top improvement areas and define actions to implement them. The goals of a Scrum retrospective include reviewing what went well and what didn’t during the sprint, identifying areas for improvement, and defining actionable steps to enhance the team's performance and process for future sprints. The focus is on continuous improvement and optimizing team effectiveness.

questions.q: A design project is ready to be transferred to production. What activity is required for phase closure? *

o.t: Determine summary budget.
Manage quality.
Ensure preventive actions are completed.
Record impacts of tailoring to any process.

questions.e: D. Record impacts of tailoring to any process Recording the impacts of tailoring to any process involves documenting how adjustments or modifications made to standard processes affect the project. This includes noting any changes made to standard practices, tools, or methodologies to better fit the specific needs of the project. Why it’s Important: Process Improvement: Understanding and recording the impacts of tailoring helps in assessing how changes to processes affect project outcomes. It provides insights into whether the tailored approach was effective or if further adjustments are needed. Future Reference: Documenting these impacts creates a reference for future projects, helping to avoid repeating mistakes or leveraging successful adaptations. Consistency and Compliance: Ensuring that tailored processes are well-documented helps maintain consistency and adherence to organizational standards, even when deviations from standard processes are made. In Context of Phase Closure: While recording the impacts of tailoring is a valuable activity, it is typically not the immediate focus for phase closure. Phase closure primarily ensures that all phase-specific tasks, like preventive actions and quality checks, are completed and documented. Recording the impacts of tailoring is more about capturing lessons learned and process adjustments for future use rather than closing out a specific project phase.

questions.q: Which of the following is not part of the Validate Release in Transition phase? *

o.t: Production deployment testing.
Active stakeholder participation.
Stakeholder satisfaction survey.
Log the deployment.

questions.e: D. Log the deployment Logging the deployment involves documenting the details of the deployment process as part of transitioning a product or solution into the production environment. This documentation is crucial for several reasons: Importance of Logging the Deployment: Audit Trail: A deployment log provides an audit trail that can be reviewed to ensure that the deployment was executed as planned. This is important for compliance, troubleshooting, and understanding the history of changes. Troubleshooting and Support: If issues arise after deployment, having a detailed log helps in diagnosing problems by providing a record of what was done, including configurations, environment details, and any issues encountered during the deployment. Knowledge Sharing: It helps in sharing knowledge with other team members or projects by providing insights into the deployment process, any adjustments made, and the outcomes of the deployment. Future Reference: The log serves as a reference for future deployments, helping to replicate successful strategies or avoid past mistakes. It can be used to improve deployment processes over time. In Context of the Validate Release in Transition Phase: During the Validate Release in Transition phase, the primary focus is on ensuring that the release is successfully integrated into the production environment. Logging the deployment is a key activity in this phase because it provides a comprehensive record of the deployment activities, ensuring that all steps are properly documented and that any issues can be tracked and addressed. In summary, logging the deployment is a fundamental part of managing and validating the transition to production, as it ensures that there is a clear record of what was done, which supports ongoing support and future improvements.

questions.q: A company that is heavily focused on delivering projects using predictive approaches on-boards a new project manager who uses hybrid approaches. The scope of the project contains a number of unclear requirements. How should the project manager plan the delivery of the project? *

o.t: Escalate the issue of unclear requirements to the management team and wait for final authorization.
Break down the requirements and prioritize the requirements into iterative work packages.
Ignore the unclear requirements and focus on the delivery plan of the project.
Wait for the requirements to be more clear before any further action is taken on the project.

questions.e: The best approach for the project manager in this situation is: B. Break down the requirements and prioritize the requirements into iterative work packages. Explanation: Breaking Down Requirements: In a hybrid approach, which combines elements of both predictive and agile methodologies, it's important to handle unclear requirements by breaking them down into smaller, more manageable pieces. This allows for incremental clarification and adaptation. Prioritizing Work Packages: By prioritizing these work packages, the project manager can focus on delivering the most critical features first. This iterative process helps address unclear requirements progressively, allowing for adjustments based on feedback and further clarifications. Benefits: Flexibility: This approach accommodates the evolving nature of requirements and allows for adjustments as more information becomes available. Risk Management: It helps mitigate risks associated with unclear requirements by addressing them in manageable chunks rather than waiting for full clarity before proceeding. Customer Feedback: Iterative delivery enables frequent feedback from stakeholders, ensuring that the evolving requirements are better aligned with customer needs.

questions.q: A project manager is concerned that team members spend too much time assisting operations and maintenance staff with a recently completed and delivered project component. The project manager has referred to the organizational process assets document to validate that the component was signed off and ownership was transferred. To which additional documents should the project manager refer? *

o.t: Procurement statement of work (SOW) and work performance report
Requirements management plan and change management plan
Procurement management plan and project charter
Final report and project document updates

questions.e: The project manager should refer to: D. Final report and project document updates Explanation: Final Report: This document typically summarizes the project’s outcomes, including whether deliverables were completed and signed off, and if the project objectives were met. It should also address the transfer of ownership and any outstanding issues or responsibilities. Project Document Updates: These include updated documentation reflecting any changes, approvals, or handovers related to the project. This documentation is crucial for verifying that all agreed-upon actions, such as the transfer of ownership and the finalization of deliverables, have been properly completed and documented.

questions.q: During project closure, the project manager finds it difficult to obtain successful project completion feedback. Some stakeholders disagree with the project's success criteria and have been frustrated with the project from the beginning. To what should the project manager refer to address these concerns? *

o.t: Project charter
Quality management plan
Scope statement
Requirements documentation

questions.e: To address concerns about the project’s success criteria and stakeholder dissatisfaction during project closure, the project manager should refer to: A. Project Charter Explanation: Project Charter: This document defines the project's objectives, scope, and success criteria. It serves as a foundational reference for understanding what was originally agreed upon regarding project success. Reviewing the project charter helps clarify whether the success criteria were clearly defined and agreed upon at the start of the project, which can assist in addressing any disagreements or frustrations from stakeholders.

questions.q: A project has components that are outsourced and the project manager is in the control phase of the procurement process. What should the project manager focus on doing? *

o.t: Finalize the contract and pay the vendors.
Develop a procurement plan and identify potential vendors.
Issue requests for proposals and select vendors.
Evaluate the performance of one of the major project vendors.

questions.e: In the control phase of the procurement process, the project manager should focus on: D. Evaluate the performance of one of the major project vendors. Explanation: Evaluate the performance of one of the major project vendors: This activity is crucial during the control phase of the procurement process. It involves assessing how well the vendors are meeting their contractual obligations and performance standards. Evaluating performance helps ensure that the outsourced components are delivered according to the agreed-upon terms and quality, and it provides a basis for taking corrective actions if necessary.

questions.q: A project team has recently finished a sprint for developing two features for a fleet management system. Although the team delivered the required features, they encountered several issues and conflicts during the sprint. Team members were upset about this experience and are now showing a lack of motivation due to what has occurred. What can the project manager do to help increase the team's motivation and engagement with the project? *

o.t: Set up one-on-one meetings with the project team members.
Review sprint progress with the project team members.
Review sprint planning procedures with the project team members.
Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members.

questions.e: To help increase the team's motivation and engagement with the project, the project manager should: D. Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members. Explanation: Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members: A sprint retrospective is a key practice in Agile methodologies that allows the team to reflect on what went well, what didn’t go well, and what could be improved. It provides a structured opportunity for the team to discuss issues, conflicts, and challenges they encountered during the sprint. This process helps identify actionable improvements, address concerns, and foster a sense of collaboration and ownership, which can boost motivation and engagement.

questions.q: A new project manager joins a project during the delivery of a critical milestone. This project has multiple stakeholders, and each has a different level of interest. The project manager needs to determine how much detail to provide to the stakeholders about the delivery. To which document should the project manager refer? *

o.t: Communications management plan
Stakeholder register
Stakeholder engagement plan
Project management plan

questions.e: C. Stakeholder engagement plan focuses on how to effectively engage stakeholders throughout the project. It includes strategies for managing stakeholder expectations, fostering relationships, and ensuring that stakeholders are appropriately involved in the project. Here’s why it may not be the most appropriate choice for determining the level of detail to provide about a critical milestone: Stakeholder Engagement Plan: Purpose: The primary goal of a stakeholder engagement plan is to outline how to interact with stakeholders, manage their expectations, and address their concerns. It involves strategies for engagement, such as how to involve stakeholders in decision-making processes and how to address their needs and concerns. Content: It details methods and strategies for engaging with stakeholders and may include aspects such as communication frequency, feedback mechanisms, and involvement strategies. However, it is generally more focused on engagement tactics rather than the specifics of communication content. Level of Detail: While the stakeholder engagement plan helps in understanding how to involve stakeholders and manage their involvement, it does not typically specify the level of detail or the content of communication for different types of project updates. It may outline general communication approaches but may not provide explicit guidance on how much detail to share about specific project milestones. Why It’s Less Suitable for Determining Communication Details: Focus on Engagement: The plan is more concerned with how to keep stakeholders engaged and satisfied rather than detailing the specifics of what information should be communicated. Communication Content: It might not include detailed guidelines about the content and level of detail required for different communications, especially for specific project milestones. In contrast, the communications management plan is specifically designed to address these concerns by providing detailed instructions on the content, frequency, and methods of communication tailored to different stakeholder needs.

questions.q: A complex project has multiple participants. The project manager agrees with the team that they need to better understand the perspective of all project participants for the optimal success of the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the stakeholder analysis.
Create a communication plan.
Conduct a SWOT analysis.
Perform a risk analysis.

questions.e: A. Review the stakeholder analysis. Explanation: Stakeholder Analysis is the process of identifying and analyzing stakeholders to understand their interests, influence, and needs regarding the project. This analysis helps the project manager and team understand the perspectives of various participants and stakeholders, which is crucial for optimizing the project’s success. Here’s why this is the best choice: Understanding Perspectives: The stakeholder analysis provides insights into who the stakeholders are, what their interests and concerns are, and how they might affect or be affected by the project. This understanding is essential for addressing their needs and expectations effectively. Identifying Influence: It helps in recognizing the level of influence each stakeholder has on the project. Knowing this can guide the project manager in prioritizing engagement and communication efforts. Tailoring Engagement: By reviewing the stakeholder analysis, the project manager can tailor communication and engagement strategies to address specific needs, concerns, and expectations, ensuring better alignment and project success.

questions.q: A long-term agile project has just reached its midway mark and a new project manager is appointed to take over. Additional to the project manager, a current stakeholder was interchanged with another who has more experience regarding the projects’ technology. What next step should the project manager take? *

o.t: Discuss expectations from the stakeholder and revise the engagement plan accordingly.
Encourage the new stakeholder to convene with the product owner to review pertinent information.
Notify all stakeholders after revising the project plan with new contents added.
Hold all upcoming sprint review meetings with the new stakeholder in attendance and revise the project plan.

questions.e: B. Encourage the new stakeholder to convene with the product owner to review pertinent information. Explanation: Encouraging the new stakeholder to meet with the product owner is a valuable step in onboarding the new stakeholder into the project. This action serves several purposes: Information Transfer: The new stakeholder needs to understand the project’s current status, goals, and specific details about the technology and requirements. Meeting with the product owner ensures they receive comprehensive and accurate information directly from the person who has been closely involved with the project’s development. Alignment on Objectives: The product owner can help the new stakeholder align with the project's objectives, priorities, and deliverables. This meeting provides a chance to clarify any uncertainties and establish a common understanding. Leverage Experience: The product owner, who is already familiar with the project, can guide the new stakeholder on how their experience can be best utilized and how they can contribute effectively.

questions.q: A project team uses the influence/commitment matrix to identify key stakeholders and prioritize them for specific action planning. For a specific group, the project team plans to keep them informed and feed them with any “early win” good news about the project. In which quadrant of the matrix are they located? *

o.t: Low Influence / Low Commitment
Low Influence / High Commitment
High Influence / Low Commitment
High Influence / High Commitment

questions.e: In the influence/commitment matrix, the group described as being kept informed and fed with “early win” good news is located in: B. Low Influence / High Commitment Explanation: The influence/commitment matrix helps in prioritizing stakeholders based on their level of influence over the project and their commitment to it. Here’s how the quadrants are defined: Low Influence / Low Commitment (A): Stakeholders with minimal impact and interest. They are not prioritized for frequent updates or engagement. Low Influence / High Commitment (B): Stakeholders who are committed to the project but do not have significant influence. Keeping them informed and sharing positive updates helps maintain their enthusiasm and support. High Influence / Low Commitment (C): Stakeholders who have significant influence but are not strongly committed. Engaging them to increase their commitment is crucial. High Influence / High Commitment (D): Stakeholders who are both influential and committed. They should be closely engaged and consulted regularly. Rationale for Option B: Low Influence / High Commitment: These stakeholders are committed to the project and value positive news, even though they do not have substantial influence over its outcomes. By keeping them informed and sharing early successes, you reinforce their support and ensure they remain engaged. Thus, stakeholders in this quadrant benefit from being kept informed and updated with positive developments to maintain their support and enthusiasm.

questions.q: Following the start of a sprint, a key stakeholder constructed an email to a project team voicing displeasure of the work that just commenced, despite being inexperienced in agile. The stakeholder is insistent about changing the internal and external deliverables. What next step should the project manager take? *

o.t: Request the team’s assessment of the matter at the next standup meeting.
Change the backlog and comply with the stakeholder’s request.
Facilitate a meeting with the product owner and the key stakeholder to align on deliverables.
Encourage the stakeholder to participate in a discussion regarding backlog clarification.

questions.e: In this situation, the most appropriate next step for the project manager is: C. Facilitate a meeting with the product owner and the key stakeholder to align on deliverables. Explanation: When a key stakeholder who is inexperienced in Agile expresses dissatisfaction and requests changes, it’s important to handle the situation carefully to ensure alignment and maintain project stability. Here’s why option C is the best choice: Facilitate a meeting with the product owner and the key stakeholder: This approach addresses the stakeholder’s concerns directly and aligns them with the product owner. The product owner is responsible for managing the backlog and prioritizing work, and the meeting can help clarify why certain decisions were made and how changes might impact the project. This dialogue ensures that stakeholder feedback is properly evaluated and integrated into the project in a way that aligns with Agile practices.

questions.q: While executing a project that is nearly behind schedule, a project manager must commission a new piece of equipment. Two local parties who will be impacted by this commission ask that the project be stopped immediately because they were not given an opportunity to provide project approval. How would implementing a stakeholder engagement plan have helped the project manager avoid this situation? *

o.t: By using the conflict management techniques described in the plan, the project manager could have gotten approval from the local parties.
Including the local parties in the plan would have ensured their sign-off and approval of the project charter.
By understanding the local parties' expectations, the project manager could have used appropriate negotiating techniques to engage them.
By identifying the local parties as stakeholders, they would have been included in relevant communications.

questions.e: In this scenario, implementing a stakeholder engagement plan would have helped the project manager avoid the situation by: D. By identifying the local parties as stakeholders, they would have been included in relevant communications. Explanation: A well-structured stakeholder engagement plan helps ensure that all relevant stakeholders are identified and their interests and concerns are addressed throughout the project. Here’s how option D addresses the issue: Identifying stakeholders: The plan would have included a process for identifying all relevant stakeholders, including local parties who might be impacted by the commissioning of new equipment. By recognizing them as stakeholders early on, the project manager would have ensured they were included in communication and approval processes. Relevant communications: Including stakeholders in relevant communications means keeping them informed and involved in decision-making processes that affect them. This would have given the local parties an opportunity to voice their concerns and provide input before major decisions were made, such as commissioning new equipment.

questions.q: A new project stakeholder is identified who has interest in, but little authority or influence on, the project. How should the project manager handle this stakeholder? *

o.t: Provide information to the stakeholder as needed.
Work closely with the stakeholder to proactively address their concerns.
Keep track of the stakeholder and respond to their needs.
Include the stakeholder on standard updates and keep them satisfied.

questions.e: For a stakeholder who has interest in but little authority or influence on the project, the project manager should handle them by: A. Provide information to the stakeholder as needed. Explanation: This approach aligns with the stakeholder's level of authority and influence. Here’s why option A is appropriate: Interest without Authority: Since the stakeholder has interest but little authority, they do not require extensive involvement or active management. Providing information as needed ensures they are kept informed but does not overextend resources on engagement efforts that might not be necessary. Efficient Resource Use: This approach is efficient in managing resources, focusing efforts on stakeholders with higher influence and authority while still addressing the needs of those with less impact.

questions.q: What is the reason for relationship network change? *

o.t: Roles and titles are formally assigned
Evolves over time as people gain and lose influence
Built-in advance by corporate management
Visible to everyone in the organization

questions.e: The reason for a relationship network change is: B. Evolves over time as people gain and lose influence Explanation: Relationship networks within organizations are dynamic and can change due to various factors, including shifts in influence, power, and roles among individuals. Here’s why option B is correct: Evolving Influence: As people’s roles, responsibilities, and levels of influence change over time, their positions in relationship networks can shift. This ongoing evolution affects how relationships are structured and how individuals interact with each other.

questions.q: A project stakeholder has been missing scheduled facilitation workshops and has delegated assigned tasks to another member of the stakeholder community. What should the project manager do to engage this stakeholder? *

o.t: Review with the stakeholder the roles and responsibilities of everyone involved as specified in the project charter.
Explain to the stakeholder the differences among the tasks assigned to each project team member.
Ask the program manager to brief this stakeholder and to require the stakeholder's attendance at all relevant meetings.
Pair the stakeholder with a more experienced team member who can act as a mentor.

questions.e: The project manager should: A. Review with the stakeholder the roles and responsibilities of everyone involved as specified in the project charter. Explanation: Reviewing the roles and responsibilities helps clarify expectations and ensures that the stakeholder understands their involvement and obligations in the project. Here’s why this option is effective: Clarifies Expectations: It helps reaffirm what is expected of the stakeholder and their role in the project, addressing any misunderstandings or miscommunications that may have led to missed workshops and delegation of tasks. Reinforces Accountability: By reviewing the roles and responsibilities as specified in the project charter, the project manager ensures that the stakeholder is aware of their commitments and the importance of their participation in the project.

questions.q: A senior manager informs a project manager that the project is not performing as well as other projects. What can the project manager use to improve performance for the next series of iterations? *

o.t: Retrospective session
Backlog analysis
Team building
Team motivation

questions.e: The project manager should use: A. Retrospective session Explanation: A retrospective session is a key practice in Agile methodologies that focuses on reflecting on the completed iterations to identify what went well, what didn’t, and how the team can improve. Here’s why it’s the best choice: Identify Issues and Improvements: During a retrospective, the team can openly discuss performance issues and challenges, allowing them to identify specific areas for improvement and develop actionable plans to address them. Continuous Improvement: Retrospectives are designed to foster a culture of continuous improvement by enabling teams to learn from their experiences and apply those lessons to future iterations.

questions.q: An organization recently updated its strategic plan and some of the changes were substantial. During a meeting for an ongoing project, an important stakeholder questioned how the project aligned with the new strategic plan. What should the project manager do first to address this concern effectively? *

o.t: Review and revise the project charter to ensure alignment with organizational strategy.
Schedule a follow-up meeting with the stakeholder to discuss their concerns.
Remind the stakeholders that the project was initiated prior to the strategy change.
Assure the stakeholder that the project is aligned with the new organizational strategy.

questions.e: The project manager should: A. Review and revise the project charter to ensure alignment with organizational strategy. Explanation: Ensure Alignment: The project charter is a foundational document that outlines the project's objectives, scope, and how it aligns with organizational goals. If there has been a substantial change in the strategic plan, it’s crucial to review and, if necessary, revise the project charter to ensure that the project continues to align with the updated strategic goals. Addressing Concerns: By reviewing and revising the project charter, the project manager can directly address the stakeholder’s concern by ensuring that the project’s objectives and direction are in line with the new strategic plan.

questions.q: Due to organizational changes, a key stakeholder is replaced by a new employee. The next status review meeting to update project progress will not take place until next month. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Schedule a separate meeting with the new stakeholder to brief them on project status.
Prepare and send a project status report to the new stakeholder for review.
Seek advice from the project sponsor on how to obtain support from the new stakeholder.
Wait for the next communication window to share information with the new stakeholder.

questions.e: The project manager should: A. Schedule a separate meeting with the new stakeholder to brief them on project status. Explanation: Proactive Communication: Scheduling a separate meeting with the new stakeholder ensures that they are quickly brought up to speed on the project's current status, key issues, and their role in the project. This proactive approach helps in establishing a strong relationship and understanding with the new stakeholder, which can be crucial for the project's success. Immediate Engagement: Waiting for the next status review meeting or only sending a report might delay the new stakeholder's understanding of the project and their ability to contribute effectively. A direct meeting provides an opportunity for interactive discussion and immediate clarification of any questions or concerns the new stakeholder might have.

questions.q: At the completion of a project, customer agreement cannot be achieved through negotiations. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Inform project team members.
Initiate litigation since all work was completed.
Start the closing phase.
Explore arbitration.

questions.e: The project manager should: D. Explore arbitration. Explanation: Resolution Through Arbitration: Arbitration is a method of resolving disputes outside of court, often involving a neutral third party who makes a binding decision. This is a suitable next step when negotiations fail, as it provides a structured process for resolving disagreements and reaching a resolution. Preserving Relationships: Arbitration can be less adversarial than litigation and can help preserve business relationships by providing a fair resolution process that both parties agree to.

questions.q: In a hybrid project, the need for customer involvement throughout the project is not understood by the customer. As a consequence, rework is beyond acceptable levels. What should the project manager do to address this issue? *

o.t: Submit a change request to obtain the required involvement from the customer.
Add this customer issue to the backlog for prioritization and review.
Meet with the customer to highlight the importance of their engagement for project success.
Instruct senior management to make the customer work closely with the team.

questions.e: The project manager should: C. Meet with the customer to highlight the importance of their engagement for project success. Explanation: Direct Communication: Meeting with the customer directly allows the project manager to explain the critical role of their involvement in the project’s success and address any misunderstandings about the need for continuous engagement. Building Understanding: This approach helps to align the customer's expectations with the project requirements and emphasizes how their involvement impacts the quality and efficiency of the project, thereby reducing rework.

questions.q: During the project kick-off meeting, the project manager announces that a hybrid approach will be used to deliver the project. Many of the team members raise a concern because they are used to working on predictive projects. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor to ensure the team is aligned with the project delivery approach.
Engage the project management office (PMO) since they identify the approach to delivering projects.
Educate the team members on agile and the benefits associated with the use of agile principles.
Change to a predictive approach to be aligned with the skills of the team members.

questions.e: The project manager should: C. Educate the team members on agile and the benefits associated with the use of agile principles. Explanation: Addressing Concerns Directly: Educating the team about agile principles helps address their concerns by providing them with the knowledge and understanding they need to adapt to the hybrid approach. This can improve their confidence and willingness to work with the new methodology. Building Buy-In: Understanding the benefits of agile and how it will be integrated with predictive elements can help the team see the value in the hybrid approach, leading to better acceptance and smoother implementation.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a Resource-Based Power in relation to mega projects? *

o.t: Recruiting on a contractual basis
Recruiting expert talents
Recruitment on the basis of secondment
Recruitment via Direct Control

questions.e: D. Recruitment via Direct Control Explanation: Resource-Based Power refers to the influence and authority that come from controlling or managing valuable resources. In the context of mega projects, resource-based power involves leveraging recruitment and resource allocation strategies to impact project success and decision-making. A. Recruiting on a contractual basis: This is a form of resource-based power as it involves using contractual agreements to influence resource availability and project management. B. Recruiting expert talents: This involves acquiring skilled individuals whose expertise can significantly impact the project's success. It reflects resource-based power by bringing in critical expertise. C. Recruitment on the basis of secondment: This involves temporarily assigning employees from other departments or organizations. It represents resource-based power by utilizing resources from outside the immediate project team. D. Recruitment via Direct Control: This term is less commonly associated with resource-based power in the context of recruitment. Direct control typically refers to the ability to manage and direct resources, but it is not specifically about recruitment methods or strategies. In contrast, the other options directly relate to recruitment practices that impact resource management in mega projects.

questions.q: What should a project manager do to obtain stakeholder agreement? *

o.t: Update Resource Management Plan
Manage Stakeholder Engagement
Monitor and Control Project Work
Schedule a meeting between sponsor and stakeholders

questions.e: B. Manage Stakeholder Engagement Explanation: To obtain stakeholder agreement, a project manager should focus on managing stakeholder engagement. This involves actively communicating with stakeholders, understanding their needs and expectations, and ensuring that their concerns and interests are addressed throughout the project. Effective stakeholder engagement helps in building relationships, gaining their support, and achieving their agreement on project deliverables and objectives. A. Update Resource Management Plan: While important for managing resources, this does not directly address obtaining stakeholder agreement. C. Monitor and Control Project Work: This is crucial for tracking project performance and ensuring alignment with objectives, but it does not specifically focus on stakeholder agreement. D. Schedule a meeting between sponsor and stakeholders: Although meetings can facilitate discussions, managing stakeholder engagement involves ongoing communication and relationship management beyond just scheduling meetings.

questions.q: A key project stakeholder showed interest in the beginning of a complex agile project but has become less involved as the sprint has progressed due to additional responsibilities. A few sprints later, the key stakeholder rejected a feature deliverable. The team is reworking the rejected deliverable for the next sprint. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Documented the project vision and objectives.
Analyzed the changes in stakeholder attributes.
Involved the key stakeholders in the decision-making process.
Customized stakeholder communications based on the stakeholders' needs.

questions.e: C. Involved the key stakeholders in the decision-making process. Explanation: To avoid the situation where a key stakeholder becomes less involved and then rejects a deliverable, the project manager should have involved the key stakeholders in the decision-making process. In Agile projects, continuous engagement of stakeholders in the decision-making process is crucial. This ensures that their expectations and requirements are consistently met and reduces the risk of rejection or dissatisfaction with deliverables. A. Documented the project vision and objectives: While important for setting the direction, this alone does not ensure stakeholder engagement throughout the project. B. Analyzed the changes in stakeholder attributes: This can provide insights into stakeholder involvement, but it does not directly address the need for active engagement and decision-making. D. Customized stakeholder communications based on the stakeholders' needs: Tailoring communications is valuable, but involving stakeholders in decision-making is more effective for ensuring their ongoing engagement and satisfaction with the deliverables.

questions.q: Which of the following is different to the other options for managing external stakeholders in mega projects? *

o.t: Persuasion
Deputation
Give and take
Strict orders

questions.e: D. Strict orders Explanation: A. Persuasion: Involves convincing stakeholders by presenting benefits or reasoning, often used in collaborative and strategic engagement. B. Deputation: Refers to delegating responsibilities or authority to others to manage stakeholder relations effectively. C. Give and take: Implies a reciprocal approach where both parties make concessions and compromises to manage relationships. D. Strict orders: This approach is more authoritarian and less collaborative. In managing external stakeholders, especially in mega projects, an authoritative approach like issuing strict orders is generally less effective and may lead to resistance or conflict, whereas persuasion, deputation, and reciprocal strategies are more collaborative and suited for effective stakeholder management.

questions.q: In managing megaprojects stakeholders, which of the following is not a resource available, as part of tactical clustering? *

o.t: Recruitment Discretion
Government Backing
Fund Discretion
Trust

questions.e: D. Trust Explanation: A. Recruitment Discretion: Refers to the ability to choose and hire the right personnel, which is a resource available for tactical clustering in managing stakeholders. B. Government Backing: Involves support or endorsement from governmental entities, which can be crucial for resource allocation and stakeholder management. C. Fund Discretion: Relates to the control over financial resources and how they are allocated, which is also a significant resource in stakeholder management. D. Trust: While trust is essential in stakeholder relationships and overall project management, it is not considered a tactical resource or a tangible asset that can be controlled or allocated like recruitment discretion, government backing, or fund discretion.

questions.q: Two stakeholders inform the project manager that the status of a critical project phase was not communicated to them. Although the project phase is in these stakeholders' area of interest, the stakeholders have only recently been identified. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Review the communications management plan.
Perform a stakeholder analysis and update the stakeholder register.
Identify new ways to send project status reports to all stakeholders.
Schedule a status meeting and invite the two new stakeholders.

questions.e: B. Perform a stakeholder analysis and update the stakeholder register. Explanation: The project manager needs to ensure that all relevant stakeholders are identified and properly documented. Since the two stakeholders have only recently been identified and were not previously included, the first step is to perform a stakeholder analysis and update the stakeholder register to include them. This will help in understanding their needs and ensuring they receive appropriate communications in the future. Once the stakeholder register is updated, the project manager can then review the communications management plan, identify new ways to communicate, and schedule meetings as needed.

questions.q: An ongoing project has a high degree of change. In order to evaluate how the IT security team will influence the performance of the project. what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Update the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix.
Analyze corporate political and power structures.
Create a project communications management plan.
Manage stakeholders' expectations.

questions.e: D. Manage stakeholders' expectations. Managing stakeholders' expectations involves ensuring that their needs and concerns are understood and addressed throughout the project lifecycle. This includes: Regular Communication: Keeping stakeholders informed about project progress, changes, and issues through consistent updates. Expectation Alignment: Ensuring that stakeholders’ expectations align with project goals, deliverables, and constraints. This may involve negotiating and clarifying what can and cannot be achieved. Feedback Mechanisms: Providing channels for stakeholders to voice their concerns or suggestions and addressing these in a timely manner. Managing Change: Handling any changes in project scope or direction that might impact stakeholder expectations, and ensuring that these changes are communicated and agreed upon. By managing stakeholders' expectations effectively, the project manager helps ensure stakeholder satisfaction and support, which is crucial for the project's success. However, in the context of evaluating how a specific team (like the IT security team) will influence project performance, updating the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix (option A) would be more directly relevant. This matrix helps in understanding the level of influence and engagement required for each stakeholder, which is critical for managing their expectations appropriately.

questions.q: In a software development project, a stakeholder wants to add a major requirement, which they feel will be a great benefit to the project. However, this requirement is not aligned to the project objectives that the business owner has documented. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Ensure the stakeholder understands the purpose of the project.
Encourage the stakeholder to follow the written business requirements.
Include the additional requirement into the project and inform the business owner.
Fast-track the project and suggest the new requirement to the business owner.

questions.e: A. Ensure the stakeholder understands the purpose of the project. When a stakeholder proposes a major requirement that does not align with the documented project objectives, it's essential first to ensure that the stakeholder understands the project’s purpose and objectives. This helps in: Clarifying Scope and Objectives: Making sure that the stakeholder comprehends how their request fits within the overall goals and constraints of the project. Managing Expectations: Helping the stakeholder understand why the requirement might not be feasible or aligned with the current objectives. Facilitating Communication: Providing a platform for discussing how the stakeholder’s ideas could potentially be addressed in future phases or through separate initiatives, if applicable. By ensuring the stakeholder understands the project’s purpose, the project manager can manage expectations and maintain alignment with the project's objectives. This approach is more effective than immediately incorporating the requirement, which could derail the project's focus or scope.

questions.q: Midway through project execution, several stakeholders raise concerns about team performance and delivery. The project manager believes the project is progressing per the approved scope, budget, and schedule. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Email the stakeholders to assure them of action.
Consult the communications management plan to manage stakeholders' expectations.
Ask the project sponsor to intervene.
Ask stakeholders to escalate their concerns to the CEO.

questions.e: B. Consult the communications management plan to manage stakeholders' expectations. The project manager should refer to the communications management plan to address stakeholder concerns. This plan outlines how to engage with stakeholders, communicate project progress, and manage their expectations effectively. By consulting this plan, the project manager can: Evaluate Communication Gaps: Determine if the stakeholders have been receiving the necessary updates and information. Reassure Stakeholders: Proactively provide clarifications or additional reports to demonstrate that the project is on track. Adjust Communication Strategy: If needed, refine the communication approach to ensure that stakeholder concerns are addressed timely and appropriately. This approach helps maintain a structured and professional response while avoiding unnecessary escalation.

questions.q: A project manager must get approval for a complex project management plan from multiple stakeholders in various countries before the project can be kicked off. The time to gain approval is limited. What should the project manager first do? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with the stakeholders and walk them through the project plan to gain their approval.
Distribute the plan to the stakeholders for their review days before scheduling a meeting to obtain approvals.
Tell the project sponsor that the stakeholder approvals will require more time and adjust the schedule.
Obtain partial stakeholder approvals and track incomplete approvals as a risk to be managed later.

questions.e: B. Distribute the plan to the stakeholders for their review days before scheduling a meeting to obtain approvals. This approach is efficient for gaining approval from multiple stakeholders across different countries within a limited timeframe. By distributing the project management plan in advance, stakeholders have the opportunity to review the details before the meeting, which helps streamline the approval process. This allows for focused discussion during the meeting, addressing any concerns or questions that might arise, and can expedite the final approval. This option ensures that the stakeholders are prepared and informed, reducing the likelihood of delays due to unfamiliarity with the content of the project plan.

questions.q: During a project's execution, a previously unidentified stakeholder within the customer's organization requests a change that could affect the project's scope. The stakeholder's influence within the customer's organization is strong. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting and, based on the outcome, update the project management plan.
Issue a change request to the change control board (CCB).
Identify the new stakeholder and update the stakeholder register.
Meet with all stakeholders to discuss the change.

questions.e: C. Identify the new stakeholder and update the stakeholder register. The first step in this scenario is to formally identify the previously unidentified stakeholder and update the stakeholder register. This is essential for understanding the stakeholder's level of influence, interest, and needs, which will help in evaluating the potential impact of their request on the project's scope. Once the stakeholder is properly documented, the project manager can better manage the situation, including determining the next steps, such as engaging with them and evaluating the change request. This ensures that the stakeholder management process is thorough and that any future engagement is aligned with the overall project strategy.

questions.q: A project is in the execution phase when the project manager realizes that several of the stakeholders identified at the start of the project were removed from the project. The stakeholders that have been removed from the project are frustrated with the unnecessary communication and express concern that the remaining stakeholders may not be receiving all of the information they require. What should the project manager have done to prevent this? *

o.t: Identified and documented all stakeholder requirements at the start of the project.
Reported all project information to every stakeholder throughout the project lifecycle.
Updated the stakeholder engagement plan through the change control process.
Relied on existing stakeholders to inform the project manager about missing stakeholders.

questions.e: C. Updated the stakeholder engagement plan through the change control process. To prevent the situation where removed stakeholders are frustrated and remaining stakeholders may not be receiving the necessary information, the project manager should have updated the stakeholder engagement plan through the change control process. This ensures that changes in stakeholder involvement are properly documented, and that communication and engagement strategies are adjusted accordingly. Regularly reviewing and updating the stakeholder engagement plan would have helped keep the right people informed while removing unnecessary communication with disengaged stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager is in the execution phase of a project. A newly identified stakeholder continuously bypasses the project manager to get feedback from the project sponsor directly, thus escalating pressure and frustration for all members of the team. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Call a project meeting of all stakeholders to discuss the matter and develop a suitable action plan.
Email the communications management plan to the stakeholder and point out that they agreed to the plan.
Meet the project sponsor and confirm that the project manager must be the single point of contact.
Meet with the stakeholder to understand their needs and update the communication management plan.

questions.e: D. Meet with the stakeholder to understand their needs and update the communication management plan. The best course of action is for the project manager to meet with the newly identified stakeholder to understand their needs and concerns. By doing this, the project manager can address the underlying reasons for bypassing and then update the communication management plan to ensure that the stakeholder’s needs are met appropriately while maintaining a clear communication flow.
