This helps to prevent further escalation and frustration while fostering better alignment between the team, stakeholders, and project sponsor.

questions.q: A project manager compiling a list of project stakeholders discovers an interested stakeholder with little to no authority. How should they manage this stakeholder? *

o.t: Keep satisfied.
Manage closely.
Monitor.
Keep informed.

questions.e: D. Keep informed. When a stakeholder has an interest in the project but has little to no authority, the appropriate strategy is to keep them informed. This ensures they are aware of the project's progress and relevant developments without requiring intensive management, which is typically reserved for stakeholders with higher authority or influence.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to a new project with multiple high-level stakeholders. Each stakeholder has provided their expectations for the project, and the project manager realizes some expectations conflict. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Facilitate a meeting to address and resolve conflicting expectations.
Prioritize the expectations of stakeholders with the highest authority.
Update the stakeholder register with the stakeholders' expectations.
Create a project hierarchy to manage the stakeholders' expectations.

questions.e: A. Facilitate a meeting to address and resolve conflicting expectations. The best approach when facing conflicting stakeholder expectations is to facilitate a meeting. This allows the project manager to bring stakeholders together to discuss and align on expectations, ensuring everyone is on the same page and potential issues are addressed collaboratively.

questions.q: While preparing a project charter for a new project, a project manager reviews lessons learned from previous projects. The lessons learned documents show frequent issues with low engagement levels and stakeholder misalignment on project objectives. What should the project manager do to avoid repetition of this issue in the new project? *

o.t: Allow any stakeholder to join the change control board (CCB) at any time in the project.
Include all stakeholders in the responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) for acceptance of the deliverables.
Gather all the requirements provided by every individual stakeholder and include in the work breakdown structure (WBS).
Build a common understanding among stakeholders about key deliverables described in the approved project charter.

questions.e: D. Build a common understanding among stakeholders about key deliverables described in the approved project charter. Building a common understanding among stakeholders about the key deliverables in the project charter helps to ensure alignment on project objectives and fosters stakeholder engagement. This approach addresses the issues of low engagement and misalignment that were identified in the lessons learned from previous projects.

questions.q: A project manager is preparing the charter for a software development project that will outsource 33 percent of user interface (UI) evaluation. The project manager needs software developers to identify the parts of the UI that a third-party can evaluate. However, the software functional manager believes that the project will reduce staff in the software development department and refuses to cooperate. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Meet with the functional manager to review the statement of work (SOW).
Ask the project sponsor to explain the rationale for third-party evaluation to the functional manager.
Provide a cost/benefit analysis of third-party evaluation to the functional manager.
Explain the intent of the UI evaluation to the functional manager.

questions.e: A. Meet with the functional manager to review the statement of work (SOW). Meeting with the functional manager to review the statement of work (SOW) is the best first step. It allows the project manager to clarify the scope and purpose of the third-party evaluation, address any concerns the functional manager may have, and ensure that the functional manager understands that the project is not intended to reduce staff but to focus on specific needs that can be outsourced. This collaborative approach fosters alignment and cooperation.

questions.q: A critical software development project has been in development for the past six sprints. A demonstration for stakeholders took place two days before the final sprint, in which a new stakeholder voiced that the product would not meet expectations for the market. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Discuss the matter with the project sponsor and new stakeholder and request them to fix the expectation issue.
Review the scope and plan of the project with the new stakeholder.
Review the list of required tasks with the development team and new stakeholder.
Follow the change management plan and revise the scope and plan upon the stakeholders' request.

questions.e: B. Review the scope and plan of the project with the new stakeholder. This option allows the project manager to directly address the concerns raised by the new stakeholder, understand their expectations, and review how the current project scope aligns with them. Engaging the new stakeholder in a discussion about the project scope and plan will help clarify any misalignments and provide an opportunity to adjust the project's direction if necessary. This approach fosters collaboration and can prevent future misunderstandings before any formal change requests are made.

questions.q: An intern is replacing a critical resource midway through a sprint. To help the intern get up to speed, the project manager assigns a senior engineer in the team as the intern's mentor. Two months later, the project goes into critical status, delaying the release milestone by a month. What should the project manager have done to avoid this scenario? *

o.t: Convinced the critical resource to remain on the project.
Requested an experienced resource as a replacement.
Negotiated additional time to complete the project.
Allocated additional time for mentoring.

questions.e: C. Negotiated additional time to complete the project would involve extending the project timeline to accommodate the disruption caused by the replacement of the critical resource. This approach might be considered if the project manager anticipated that the intern’s lack of experience would significantly impact the project's progress. By negotiating additional time, the project manager aims to manage the project's schedule proactively, giving the team more leeway to complete the project tasks and adjust for the delay caused by the resource change. However, while this option can be useful in managing project delays, it doesn't directly address the immediate problem of ensuring that the replacement is adequately skilled to handle the critical tasks. Ensuring that an experienced resource is in place (option B) might be a more effective strategy to prevent delays and ensure project quality, especially in critical phases.

questions.q: A key project team member is leaving the organization at the halfway point of the project. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Meet with remaining team members to reassign workloads.
Work with the functional manager to find a replacement.
Evaluate the impact of the loss of the team member on the project.
Reassess the resource roles and team composition.

questions.e: C. Evaluate the impact of the loss of the team member on the project is the best initial step. Before taking any further actions, the project manager should first assess how the departure of the key team member will affect the project in terms of tasks, deadlines, and overall project objectives. This evaluation will provide a clearer understanding of the implications and help in making informed decisions about subsequent steps, such as finding a replacement or redistributing the workload.

questions.q: During project execution, an issue arises that requires additional budget and time to resolve the issue. The project team did not identify this issue as a risk during risk management planning. The project sponsor points out that this risk has occurred on past projects. What should the project manager have done to avoid this oversight? *

o.t: Reviewed the risk management plan.
Confirmed organizational risk appetite.
Reviewed the lessons learned register.
Allocated additional contingency reserves.

questions.e: C. Reviewed the lessons learned register is the most appropriate action the project manager should have taken to avoid this oversight. By reviewing the lessons learned register from past projects, the project manager could have identified recurring issues, including risks that had materialized previously but were not documented as risks in the current project. This would have informed the risk management planning process and helped in proactively addressing similar risks.

questions.q: A team is working on a new project and the sponsor refuses to approve a budget increase needed for the current iteration. What should the project manager do to address this situation? *

o.t: Submit a change request to get formal approval for a budget increase.
Work with the stakeholders to develop flexible budgeting approaches.
Explain to the sponsor the risk of not having the budget approval.
Spend the extra money and plan to compensate in the next sprint.

questions.e: B. Work with the stakeholders to develop flexible budgeting approaches involves creating adaptable budgeting strategies to accommodate changes in project requirements or unforeseen issues. While this can be a helpful approach in managing budget constraints, it might not be the most immediate or effective solution for addressing a situation where a specific budget increase is refused by the sponsor. Here's a breakdown of why this approach may not be the best first step: Immediate Needs: When a budget increase is necessary and a sponsor refuses it, the immediate need is to address the reason for the refusal and communicate the associated risks. Developing flexible budgeting approaches is more of a long-term strategy and may not resolve the urgent issue at hand. Understanding Risks: Before working on flexible budgeting approaches, it's crucial to explain the risks and impacts of not approving the budget increase to the sponsor. This helps in making a case for why the increase is necessary. Approval Process: The process for getting budget approvals often involves formal steps. Instead of working on flexible budgeting, it is more effective to focus on gaining the sponsor’s approval by addressing their concerns and explaining the risks involved. Flexible budgeting approaches are valuable for ongoing project management and can help manage changes and uncertainties in the future, but they do not directly address the immediate need for budget approval in the current iteration. Therefore, C. Explain to the sponsor the risk of not having the budget approval is a more direct and effective approach for addressing the situation.

questions.q: During an iteration, a key project team member announces their resignation. The project manager realizes that one of the product features will be impacted by the resignation. What should the project manager do to address this situation? *

o.t: Submit a change request to modify the delivery date based on this unexpected situation.
Request that human resources (HR) retain the team member until the end of the project.
Accelerate knowledge sharing with the cross-functional team to ensure that this situation is understood.
Discuss the situation with the product owner and determine if resources should be added to the team.

questions.e: D. Discuss the situation with the product owner and determine if resources should be added to the team is a valid approach but comes after addressing the immediate impact of the resignation. Here's why discussing the situation with the product owner and considering resource addition is important: Aligns with Project Goals: The product owner can provide insights into how the resignation might affect the project’s goals and deliverables. This discussion helps ensure that any decisions about adding resources align with the project's objectives and priorities. Resource Planning: If the impact of the resignation is significant and cannot be managed through knowledge sharing alone, the product owner can help assess whether additional resources are needed to cover the gap. This might involve bringing in a new team member or redistributing tasks among existing team members. Strategic Decisions: This approach involves making strategic decisions about how to manage the impact of the resignation. It ensures that any changes to the team or project scope are carefully considered and aligned with the overall project strategy. However, while this step is important, it should follow the immediate actions: Knowledge Sharing: Ensure that knowledge from the departing team member is transferred to the remaining team members to minimize disruption and maintain continuity. Assess Immediate Impact: Understand the current impact of the resignation on the project’s tasks and milestones before making decisions about additional resources. The reason this step comes after accelerating knowledge sharing is that adding resources or making adjustments is often more effective when the team is prepared and has a clear understanding of the impact and requirements.

questions.q: During an iteration, a key project team member announces their resignation. The project manager realizes that one of the product features will be impacted by the resignation. What should the project manager do to address this situation? *

o.t: Submit a change request to modify the delivery date based on this unexpected situation.
Request that human resources (HR) retain the team member until the end of the project.
Accelerate knowledge sharing with the cross-functional team to ensure that this situation is understood.
Discuss the situation with the product owner and determine if resources should be added to the team.

questions.q: A key resource approaches the project manager after the kick-off meeting and expresses concern that they will be unable to deliver their assigned tasks due to other priorities. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Schedule a team meeting to assess and manage priorities.
Document the lack of availability as a risk in the risk register.
Escalate this issue to the project sponsor for executive support.
Update the project management plan accordingly to reflect a potential delay.

questions.e: A. Schedule a team meeting to assess and manage priorities is the most appropriate initial action in this situation. Here’s why: Immediate Assessment: A team meeting allows the project manager to quickly assess the situation with the team. This includes understanding the key resource’s concerns and any potential impacts on their tasks. It also enables the project manager to gauge the overall project impact and gather input from other team members. Collaborative Solution: Discussing the issue with the team helps in collaboratively finding solutions. It can lead to reassigning tasks, adjusting deadlines, or finding ways to manage the workload better to address the resource’s concerns while keeping the project on track. Prioritization: The meeting can help in reassessing and managing project priorities. This might involve redistributing tasks or adjusting priorities to align with the available resources and their other commitments. Immediate Action: Addressing the concern promptly with the team helps in managing the issue before it becomes a larger problem, and it can prevent the need for more drastic measures such as escalating the issue or updating the project plan due to unresolved concerns. While documenting the issue in the risk register (B), escalating to the sponsor (C), or updating the project management plan (D) are also important steps, these actions are generally more appropriate after assessing and managing the priorities through direct team engagement.

questions.q: A project manager has developed a project management plan based on agile methodologies in an effort to deliver the product quickly. However, the project is complex and the requirements are unclear, putting the schedule at risk. What should the project manager do to get the project back on track? *

o.t: Rebaseline the schedule to accept additional expectations and potential delays.
Review the product backlog with the product owner and team to resolve the status.
Increase the number of standup meetings and implement daily status updates.
Adjust the plan to employ more iterative and incremental life cycle features.

questions.e: B. Review the product backlog with the product owner and team to resolve the status is the most appropriate action to get the project back on track. Here’s why: Clarify Requirements: Reviewing the product backlog helps to clarify and prioritize the requirements. Since the requirements are unclear, this step ensures that the most important and valuable work is identified and addressed first, helping to stabilize the project’s direction. Prioritization and Planning: It allows the team to reprioritize the backlog items based on current understanding and project needs. This can help in managing the complexity and addressing any immediate issues that might be putting the schedule at risk. Team Collaboration: Engaging the team in backlog review promotes collaboration and alignment on what needs to be done. This collective effort can lead to better planning and more efficient use of resources. Manage Complexity: Addressing the backlog helps in managing the project's complexity by breaking down tasks into more manageable increments. This iterative approach is central to agile methodologies and helps in handling evolving requirements effectively. While options A, C, and D might have their own merits in different contexts, focusing on the backlog and clarifying priorities directly addresses the issues of unclear requirements and complexity in an agile project.

questions.q: During a project review, the construction manager reports that the concrete production rate has changed over the last three months. They would like to have an idea of what to expect in the next three months. What analysis should be conducted? *

o.t: Earned value analysis
Critical path analysis
Trend analysis
Cost-benefit analysis

questions.e: C. Trend analysis should be conducted in this situation. Here’s why: Trend Analysis: This involves examining data over time to identify patterns or trends. In this case, the construction manager wants to understand how the concrete production rate has changed and to predict future performance. Trend analysis will help in assessing the rate changes and making forecasts for the next three months. Historical Data: By looking at the historical data on production rates, trend analysis can provide insights into whether the changes are consistent, cyclical, or irregular, which helps in forecasting future performance. Decision Making: Understanding trends will aid in making informed decisions about production planning and resource allocation for the upcoming months. While Earned Value Analysis, Critical Path Analysis, and Cost-Benefit Analysis are important project management tools, they are not as directly relevant to forecasting based on changes in production rates. Earned Value Analysis focuses on performance relative to scope, schedule, and cost; Critical Path Analysis deals with project scheduling; and Cost-Benefit Analysis evaluates financial viability.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a hybrid project. The organization uses a risk register, but the development team considers this to be a predictive process and prefers to use a Scrum process. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Personally manage and own the risk register because this is an organizational requirement.
Delegate the responsibility of updating the risk register to the development team lead.
Ask the developers to use the risk register because this is an organizational requirement.
Consider tailoring the strategy by merging elements of the risk register and Scrum processes.

questions.e: D. Consider tailoring the strategy by merging elements of the risk register and Scrum processes. Here’s why: Hybrid Approach: In a hybrid project, it's often necessary to integrate both predictive and agile methodologies. Merging elements from both approaches allows the project to benefit from the strengths of each. Tailoring: By combining elements of the risk register with Scrum practices, you can align with organizational requirements while accommodating the development team's preference for Scrum. This ensures that the project remains compliant with organizational processes and also leverages the agile team's preferences for managing risk in a way that fits their workflow. Flexibility: Tailoring the approach helps maintain flexibility, allowing for effective risk management within the Scrum framework. For instance, the risk register can be used to document and track risks, while Scrum processes handle risk identification and mitigation as part of regular sprints and reviews. Team Buy-In: Integrating both approaches helps ensure that the development team is more engaged and receptive to the risk management process, leading to better collaboration and project outcomes.

questions.q: During an agile retrospective session, several team members mentioned that they were confused about the iteration's progress. What should the project manager do to avoid this confusion? *

o.t: Coach the team to review the iteration board.
Prepare a daily project status report and share it with the team.
Ask the team to refer to the iteration backlog report.
Address the issue at the next retrospective session.

questions.e: A. Coach the team to review the iteration board. Here's why: Visual Management: The iteration board (or Scrum board) provides a visual representation of the iteration's progress. Coaching the team to regularly review this board helps ensure that everyone has a clear and up-to-date understanding of the status of tasks and progress within the iteration. Immediate Feedback: The iteration board helps in providing immediate feedback about what’s being worked on, what’s completed, and what’s pending. This transparency can reduce confusion and improve alignment among team members. Promotes Self-Management: By encouraging the team to use the iteration board, the project manager fosters a sense of ownership and self-management. It helps team members stay informed about progress and address issues as they arise. Ongoing Practice: Addressing this confusion through the iteration board helps to integrate this practice into the team's regular routines, rather than waiting for the next retrospective session, which might be too late to resolve ongoing issues.

questions.q: After a review meeting, a scrum master repeats the importance of quality, focusing especially on the Cost of Change. Which of the following is the scrum master not referring to? *

o.t: Shorten the defect cycle time.
Fix escaped defects.
Support more features.
Reduce the technical debt.

questions.e: C. Support more features. Here's why: Cost of Change: In the context of agile and Scrum, the Cost of Change generally refers to the impact and expenses associated with addressing defects and technical debt, as well as the potential delays and extra work required when changes are made later in the development process. Shorten the defect cycle time: This is relevant because reducing the time it takes to address and fix defects lowers the overall cost of change by resolving issues more quickly. Fix escaped defects: This is also relevant as fixing defects that were not caught early in the process often incurs higher costs and impacts the project more significantly. Reduce the technical debt: Addressing technical debt helps minimize future changes and complications, thereby reducing the cost of change over time. Support more features: While adding features is important, it is not directly related to managing the cost of change. Supporting more features does not necessarily address the issues related to the cost of managing defects and technical debt.

questions.q: An agile project is in its last iteration. During the daily standup, the team realizes that they will not be able to complete all the activities that were planned for the sprint. The team members create a contingency plan. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Discuss the contingency plan with the product owner.
Discuss the contingency plan with stakeholders.
Discuss the contingency plan with the project sponsor.
Execute the contingency plan immediately.

questions.e: A. Discuss the contingency plan with the product owner. Here's why: Discuss the contingency plan with the product owner: In Agile, especially in Scrum, the product owner is crucial for prioritizing the backlog and making decisions about scope changes. The product owner needs to be informed about any changes or contingency plans that might affect the deliverables and the project's overall goals. Discuss the contingency plan with stakeholders: While it’s important to keep stakeholders informed, the immediate step after creating a contingency plan should involve the product owner, who directly manages the project’s scope and priorities. Discuss the contingency plan with the project sponsor: The project sponsor should be informed of major changes, but the product owner should be the first to review and address the implications of the contingency plan. Execute the contingency plan immediately: Execution of the contingency plan should be preceded by discussion and alignment with the product owner to ensure it is in line with project goals and priorities.

questions.q: A customer requested a change in functionality for a product that will be delivered in the next sprint. The responsible specialist for this change is also assigned to a deliverable for another project. The project manager needs to negotiate the availability of the specialist. Who is responsible for confirming the specialist's availability? *

o.t: Project sponsor
Functional manager
Product owner
Human resources

questions.e: B. Functional manager Here’s why: Functional manager: The functional manager oversees resources within their department or function and is responsible for managing resource allocation and availability. They are the right person to negotiate the availability of the specialist across different projects. Project sponsor: The project sponsor provides high-level support and resources for the project but does not typically manage day-to-day resource allocation. Product owner: The product owner is responsible for the product backlog and prioritization but does not handle resource management. Human resources: HR manages recruitment, training, and administrative aspects of employees but is not typically involved in the detailed negotiation of project-specific resource availability.

questions.q: Due to a recent incident, a dissatisfied stakeholder files a complaint about a project that has been closed. What can the project manager do to help resolve this? *

o.t: Execute the relationship management plan.
Consult with the project sponsor to manage the dissatisfied stakeholder.
Review the project management information system (PMIS) archives.
Update the risk register.

questions.e: C. Review the project management information system (PMIS) archives. Here's why: Review the PMIS archives: Checking the PMIS archives helps the project manager understand the history of the project, including decisions, communications, and issues that may have contributed to the complaint. This information can be crucial in resolving the issue by providing context and details. Execute the relationship management plan: While this might be relevant in some situations, the project is already closed, and the relationship management plan is typically used during active project management, not after closure. Consult with the project sponsor: The sponsor might be involved in resolving the issue, but the first step should be to review project records to understand the context before escalating. Update the risk register: This is not applicable as the project is closed, and the risk register is used for managing risks during the project's lifecycle.

questions.q: During the testing phase of a project, a team member finds that some requirements were not met. If the project now adds work to meet the requirements, it may cause a large time and cost overrun. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to top management.
Perform an impact analysis.
Call for a stakeholder meeting.
Update the risk register.

questions.e: B. Perform an impact analysis. Here's why: Perform an impact analysis: This is the first step to understand the full consequences of adding the work required to meet the unmet requirements. The impact analysis will help the project manager assess the potential effects on time, cost, and scope, providing a basis for making informed decisions about how to address the issue. Escalate the issue to top management: While escalation might be necessary later, performing an impact analysis is crucial for understanding the specifics before involving top management. Call for a stakeholder meeting: Stakeholder involvement might be needed to discuss the findings and potential actions, but it’s essential to first have a clear understanding of the impact. Update the risk register: The risk register might need updating later, but the immediate priority is to analyze the impact of the issue.

questions.q: During a product acceptance test for a software project, the project sponsor tells the project manager that the software will only pass if the theme color is changed from red to blue. The project manager reviewed the planning documents and confirmed that the theme color should be red. The sponsor insists that the color be changed to blue. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Suggest that the project sponsor submit a formal change request to change the requirement for the theme.
Tell the project sponsor to accept the theme because the contract clearly states it should be red.
Agree with the project sponsor and change the theme color as requested to avoid potential conflict.
Request that procurement change the theme color to blue to align with the project sponsor's expectations.

questions.e: A. Suggest that the project sponsor submit a formal change request to change the requirement for the theme. Here's why: Suggest that the project sponsor submit a formal change request: This ensures that any changes to the project scope are formally documented and approved through the established change control process. This approach maintains project control and ensures that any changes are assessed for impact on the project’s schedule, cost, and resources. Tell the project sponsor to accept the theme because the contract clearly states it should be red: This might lead to conflict or dissatisfaction. It doesn’t address the possibility of the sponsor’s needs being valid or changeable. Agree with the project sponsor and change the theme color as requested: While this might resolve the immediate issue, it bypasses formal change management procedures and could lead to scope creep and potential project issues. Request that procurement change the theme color to blue: This action is premature and skips the formal process required to handle changes in project requirements.

questions.q: A project manager is managing an agile project which has many risks identified in the risk register. The current sprint deals with a critical aspect of the project. During the iteration, an identified risk occurs which ceases project development. The project manager logs the risk occurrence. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Raise the frequency of communications and leverage stakeholders to assist in resolving issues.
Assign responsibility for the communication management plan to a senior team member.
Invite the stakeholders to the next retrospective meeting and inform them of the issue.
Delay development of the critical aspect to the next sprint and work on items currently in the backlog

questions.e: A. Raise the frequency of communications and leverage stakeholders to assist in resolving issues. Here's why: Raise the frequency of communications and leverage stakeholders to assist in resolving issues: In an agile project, effective communication and stakeholder engagement are crucial for addressing and resolving issues quickly. Raising the frequency of communications helps keep everyone informed and involved in resolving the issue that is impacting project development. Assign responsibility for the communication management plan to a senior team member: This is a reactive measure and might not address the immediate need for handling the current risk and its impact on the project. Invite the stakeholders to the next retrospective meeting and inform them of the issue: While this is important for reflecting on the issue, it may not provide immediate resolution to the current problem that is halting development. Delay development of the critical aspect to the next sprint and work on items currently in the backlog: This approach might lead to delays and does not address how to resolve the risk that has caused the halt in the current sprint. The focus should be on managing and mitigating the issue promptly.

questions.q: A project manager identifies that the work started by the project team is inconsistent with industry regulations. What should the project manager update? *

o.t: Organizational process assets
Work performance data
Issue log
Project management plan

questions.e: C. Issue log Here's why: Issue log: The issue log is used to track and manage issues that arise during the project, including inconsistencies with industry regulations. By updating the issue log, the project manager can document the problem, track its resolution, and ensure it is addressed appropriately. Organizational process assets: These are resources and practices used by the organization, such as templates and guidelines, but updating them is not the immediate action for addressing project-specific issues. Work performance data: This reflects the actual performance of the project work but does not directly address regulatory inconsistencies. Project management plan: While the project management plan may need to be updated to address changes required due to regulatory issues, the initial step is to document the inconsistency in the issue log for tracking and resolution.

questions.q: A project manager has just taken over an ongoing project. The previous project manager resigned from the organization. During a review of the project documentation, the project manager realizes there are major deviations in the procurement process used by the previous project manager to engage service providers currently working on the project. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Call the previous project manager to understand the rationale for the abnormal procurement process.
Contact the service providers to discuss the deviation and demand that they resolve the issue.
Report the service providers and the previous project manager to the ethics committee of the organization.
Flag the abnormal procurement process as a critical issue for the attention of senior management.

questions.e: D. Flag the abnormal procurement process as a critical issue for the attention of senior management. Here's why: Flag the abnormal procurement process as a critical issue for the attention of senior management: This approach ensures that senior management is aware of the deviations and can take appropriate action. It is crucial for addressing potential compliance issues, assessing the impact on the project, and deciding on the next steps, which may include rectifying the process or making necessary adjustments. Call the previous project manager to understand the rationale for the abnormal procurement process: Since the previous project manager has resigned, reaching out might not be feasible or effective in resolving the issue. Contact the service providers to discuss the deviation and demand that they resolve the issue: While it might be necessary to address deviations with the service providers, this action should follow a formal review and escalation to ensure that it aligns with organizational policies and that senior management is informed. Report the service providers and the previous project manager to the ethics committee of the organization: This is a more severe action that may be premature. The priority should be to assess and address the issue through appropriate channels before considering reporting to the ethics committee.

questions.q: A new project manager resumes a project in its execution phase. During a project status meeting, a team member reports an issue shared by a stakeholder. What should the new project manager do? *

o.t: Review the issue log.
Immediately address the issue.
Review the stakeholder engagement plan.
Update the risk management plan.

questions.e: A. Review the issue log. Here's why: Review the issue log: This is the appropriate first step because the issue log should contain details about the reported issue, including its history, current status, and any previous actions taken. Reviewing the issue log will provide the new project manager with context and help determine the next steps for addressing the issue. Immediately address the issue: While it’s important to address the issue, doing so without first understanding its context and history could lead to ineffective or redundant actions. Review the stakeholder engagement plan: This is useful for understanding stakeholder expectations and communication needs but doesn’t directly address the specific issue reported by the team member. Update the risk management plan: This is relevant if the issue is related to a risk that was not previously identified. However, updating the risk management plan is a follow-up action after understanding the issue’s impact and relevance.

questions.q: While executing a critical iterative phase of a project, a problem previously identified as a risk just became a confirmed issue, which has halted progress. After entering the new item in the issue log, what should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Increase communications and involve stakeholders in the resolution whenever necessary.
Change the communications management plan and assign ownership to a team member.
Escalate the issue within the team during the next project retrospective meeting.
Add the issue to the product backlog to bring it into focus during the current sprint.

questions.e: A. Increase communications and involve stakeholders in the resolution whenever necessary. Here's why: Increase communications and involve stakeholders in the resolution whenever necessary: This is the most appropriate next step because effective communication is crucial for addressing and resolving issues, especially when they halt progress. Involving stakeholders can help to ensure that all relevant parties are aware of the issue, its impact, and any required actions. This approach also facilitates collaborative problem-solving and can provide additional resources or support needed to resolve the issue. Change the communications management plan and assign ownership to a team member: While this may be necessary if the current plan is inadequate, it is not the immediate next step after identifying and logging the issue. The focus should be on resolving the issue first. Escalate the issue within the team during the next project retrospective meeting: Retrospectives are typically used for reflecting on past performance and processes. Escalating an issue in this context might delay the resolution since the meeting may not occur immediately. Add the issue to the product backlog to bring it into focus during the current sprint: This approach is more relevant for product backlog items and may not address the urgent need for resolution in the current iteration. Additionally, it might not involve stakeholders in the immediate resolution of the issue.

questions.q: A project is estimated to have a total of 250 story points. The team planned 40 story points for each iteration and delivered 40, 10, 20, and 15 story points in the first four iterations. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Reassign undelivered tasks to team members to complete during the next iteration.
Work with team members to adjust the planned story points for the next iterations.
Remove the features that cannot be delivered from the product backlog and update the customer.
Negotiate with the customer for an extension of the deliverables due to holiday schedules.

questions.e: B. Work with team members to adjust the planned story points for the next iterations. Here's why: Work with team members to adjust the planned story points for the next iterations: This approach is most appropriate because it involves reassessing and recalibrating the team's planning based on their actual performance. The team has delivered fewer story points than planned in the first four iterations, which suggests that the original estimates might have been overly optimistic. Adjusting the planned story points can help set more realistic goals for future iterations, improving the likelihood of meeting project objectives. Reassign undelivered tasks to team members to complete during the next iteration: This might help in addressing specific tasks, but it does not address the broader issue of planning accuracy and iteration performance. Remove the features that cannot be delivered from the product backlog and update the customer: This is a more drastic measure and may not be necessary if the issue is related to planning accuracy rather than the scope of work. Negotiate with the customer for an extension of the deliverables due to holiday schedules: While negotiating extensions might be needed in some cases, it should be considered only after understanding and addressing the root cause of the delivery issues.

questions.q: Common problems during project scope definition are internal and external dependencies. Which of the following is a dependency that can add complexity to the project? *

o.t: Non-dependency between a project and the overall program.
Underfunded projects that are dependent upon external resources.
Non-dependency of the project upon an environment in which it is designed to be functional.
Over-staffed project with extra capacity.

questions.e: B. Underfunded projects that are dependent upon external resources. Here’s why: Underfunded projects that are dependent upon external resources: This situation introduces complexity because the project relies on external resources that may not be adequately funded or available. The lack of funding can lead to delays, increased costs, and difficulties in meeting project objectives, adding significant complexity to the project. Non-dependency between a project and the overall program: While dependencies can be complex, a lack of dependency does not inherently add complexity to the project itself. Non-dependency of the project upon an environment in which it is designed to be functional: If a project is not dependent on its intended environment, it may not align with its intended goals, but this is not typically an issue of dependency complexity. Over-staffed project with extra capacity: Having extra capacity might lead to inefficiencies but does not add complexity related to dependencies.

questions.q: During testing of a project component, a senior tester discovers a functionality that will ensure the future performance of the project's solution. This will create a change in scope. Which type of change request should be made to include this functionality? *

o.t: Preventive action
Corrective action
Defect repair
Scope update

questions.e: A.Preventive action is a type of change request or action taken to prevent potential problems or issues from occurring in the future. This action is aimed at reducing the likelihood of risks or issues by addressing potential causes before they impact the project. Here's how it relates to project changes: Purpose: Preventive actions are used to avoid problems rather than correct them after they arise. They focus on anticipating and mitigating risks before they become actual issues. Example: If a project team identifies a potential risk of performance degradation due to a component’s design, they might implement preventive measures to ensure that the design is robust and can handle the expected load. This might include additional testing or redesigning parts of the component to address potential weaknesses. In the context of your scenario: The change in functionality discovered by the senior tester is an enhancement or addition to the project scope, not a preventive measure. The correct type of change request for including new functionality is a scope update, as it involves altering the project scope to incorporate new features or changes that were not initially planned.

questions.q: A project manager is working on requirement management in a pharmaceutical company. Which improvement is something the project manager's organization should expect as an outcome of the project? *

o.t: Reduced quality
Increased costs
Reduced risks
Increased schedule

questions.e: In a pharmaceutical company, effective requirement management aims to ensure that the project meets regulatory standards and quality expectations. The expected outcome of effective requirement management should be: C. Reduced risks Here’s why: Reduced Risks: By effectively managing requirements, the project manager ensures that all requirements are well-defined, validated, and adhered to. This helps to avoid misunderstandings, scope creep, and compliance issues, all of which can reduce project risks and increase the likelihood of meeting project goals and regulatory requirements. Increased Costs and Schedule: While good requirement management might lead to better cost control and adherence to schedule, these are not direct improvements; they are more related to how well the requirements are managed rather than being direct outcomes of requirement management itself. Reduced Quality: Effective requirement management should aim to maintain or improve quality, not reduce it. So, reduced risks is the most appropriate expected outcome of effective requirement management in this context.

questions.q: A project team discovers an opportunity to enhance software without impacting the budget or schedule. The team makes the enhancement without proper documentation, which later causes production issues. What process should have been conducted to prevent this? *

o.t: Control Schedule
Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis
Plan Scope Management
Perform Integrated Change Control

questions.e: To prevent issues caused by undocumented changes or enhancements, the process that should have been conducted is: D. Perform Integrated Change Control Here's why: Perform Integrated Change Control: This process ensures that any changes to the project are properly documented, reviewed, and approved before implementation. It helps to maintain control over project changes, including enhancements, and ensures that they do not impact the project's objectives, schedule, or budget without proper consideration. This process includes assessing the impact of changes, obtaining approval from relevant stakeholders, and updating project documents and plans accordingly. Control Schedule: This process is focused on managing changes to the project schedule and does not cover changes to the project scope or enhancements specifically. Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis: This process involves assessing risks in terms of their impact and probability but does not directly address the management and documentation of changes. Plan Scope Management: This process is about defining how scope changes will be managed but does not involve the actual control and documentation of changes during execution. Thus, Perform Integrated Change Control is the correct process to manage and prevent issues related to undocumented changes or enhancements.

questions.q: A new product was accepted by the customer, but after two weeks the project manager received a complaint from the customer saying that the product's functionality requirements were not met. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.
Review the scope validation process.
Schedule an inspection of the product.
Validate the scope with the customer.

questions.e: B. Review the scope validation process is a valid approach in this situation, but it is not the immediate first step. Here's an explanation of why reviewing the scope validation process is relevant: Scope Validation Process Scope Validation is the process of formalizing acceptance of the completed project deliverables. It involves checking that the deliverables meet the specified requirements and are approved by the customer or sponsor. In the context of your scenario: Ensuring Requirements Alignment: If the customer claims that the functionality requirements were not met, it is crucial to review how the scope validation was conducted to understand if there were any lapses or misunderstandings during this process. This could help in identifying whether the issue is with the product itself or with how the requirements were communicated and accepted. Identifying Process Gaps: By reviewing the scope validation process, the project manager can identify any potential gaps or weaknesses in how requirements were gathered, documented, and validated. This can provide insights into whether the issue is due to a procedural oversight or an actual discrepancy in the deliverables. Improving Future Projects: If the scope validation process was flawed, addressing these issues can improve the validation process for future projects, ensuring that requirements are properly met and accepted. Why It’s Not the First Step Understanding the Current Issue: Before reviewing the process, the project manager should first understand the specific nature of the complaint by validating the scope with the customer. This helps in determining whether the problem lies with the delivered product or the validation process itself. Effective Resolution: Directly addressing the customer's complaint by validating the scope with them will provide immediate clarity on whether the product meets the agreed-upon requirements. If the complaint is validated, then the process review can follow to identify and correct any procedural flaws. In summary, while reviewing the scope validation process is important for understanding and improving how requirements are managed, the first step should be to validate the scope with the customer to understand the current issue clearly. This will then guide whether the scope validation process needs to be revisited or if other corrective actions are required.

questions.q: A project manager learns that a few stakeholders have a disagreement regarding the results of one project deliverable. What is the next step the project manager should take? *

o.t: Review and analyze the project requirements document.
Review the approved version of a scope statement.
Organize a meeting with the stakeholders.
Modernize documented project risks and their responses.

questions.e: C. Organize a meeting with the stakeholders is the most appropriate next step in this scenario. Here's why: Explanation Direct Communication: Organizing a meeting with the stakeholders allows the project manager to directly address the disagreement and understand the specific concerns and viewpoints of each stakeholder. This facilitates open communication and helps in resolving conflicts effectively. Clarifying Issues: In the meeting, the project manager can clarify any misunderstandings and ensure that all stakeholders have a shared understanding of the deliverable. This can help in identifying whether the disagreement is due to miscommunication, differing expectations, or other issues. Consensus Building: A meeting provides an opportunity for stakeholders to discuss their concerns and reach a consensus or compromise on the deliverable. This can help in aligning all parties and moving forward with the project.

questions.q: A project team completes the identification of project and product requirements. Which of the following were used to accomplish this? *

o.t: Benchmarking, network diagram, and trend analysis
Work breakdown structure (WBS), trend analysis, and observation/conversation
Brainstorming, affinity diagrams, and mind mapping
Affinity diagrams, benchmarking, and observation/conversation

questions.e: C. Brainstorming, affinity diagrams, and mind mapping are commonly used techniques to identify project and product requirements. Here’s why: Explanation Brainstorming: This technique involves generating a wide range of ideas and solutions through group discussion. It is useful for identifying all possible requirements and gathering diverse input from stakeholders and team members. Affinity Diagrams: This tool helps in organizing ideas into groups based on their natural relationships. It is often used to categorize and prioritize requirements by grouping similar items together, making it easier to identify and manage them. Mind Mapping: This technique visually represents information and relationships. It helps in organizing and structuring requirements by connecting related ideas and concepts, which can aid in understanding and defining the scope of the project.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a new software development project and has met with the customer to discuss their requirements. The customer has provided the project manager with a list of requirements, but did not differentiate the technical requirements from the customer requirements. Which of the following requirements should the project manager classify as a customer requirement? *

o.t: The software should be able to process 1000 transactions per second.
The software should use a secure database encryption algorithm.
The software should be able to run on a variety of operating systems.
The software should be easy to use and navigate.

questions.e: D. The software should be easy to use and navigate. Explanation Customer Requirements are typically those that focus on the user experience, functionality from the user's perspective, and overall usability. They represent what the customer wants the software to achieve from a practical and user-centric viewpoint. Technical Requirements, on the other hand, are specifications that detail how the system should be built to meet the customer requirements. These are usually more focused on technical aspects and

questions.q: A project manager is involved in a project where requirements are constantly evolving. What should the project manager do to achieve success? *

o.t: Provide regular updates and request deliverable-based approvals from the product owner.
Work with the team to ensure they are on track and delivering on schedule.
Maintain a comfortable working atmosphere to improve team cohesion.
Ensure documentation and processes are filed appropriately and update the product owner.

questions.e: The correct answer is A. Provide regular updates and request deliverable-based approvals from the product owner. In a project with constantly evolving requirements, it is important to maintain regular communication with the product owner and ensure deliverable-based approvals. This allows the project to remain aligned with the changing requirements and ensures that progress is consistently validated.

questions.q: A project manager works for a global company and understands the importance of the requirement management plan. When should the requirement management plan be implemented? *

o.t: At the start of the project
Prior to executing
After customer contract signature
During the planning phase

questions.e: ption A. At the start of the project implies that the requirements management plan should be implemented right at the beginning of the project, even before the planning phase. However, this is not accurate because the requirements management plan is typically developed during the planning phase, after the project has been initiated and key objectives have been outlined. At the start of the project, the focus is on initiation tasks, such as defining the project charter and identifying stakeholders. The detailed processes for managing requirements are best established during the planning phase when more information is available.

questions.q: The sponsor of a hybrid project wants to see a more detailed breakdown in the project charter, not just the milestones. The project manager informs the sponsor that preparing the breakdown will require two more iterations. Why is this additional time required? *

o.t: The milestone schedule was prepared based on the project manager's experience only.
The steering committee has to review and approve the schedule first.
Scope in the charter should be approved before detail planning with the team can occur.
Schedule details are only planned one iteration in advance in a hybrid approach.

questions.e: Option C. Scope in the charter should be approved before detail planning with the team can occur suggests that the project scope needs formal approval before the project manager can begin detailed planning with the team. In project management, the project charter defines the initial scope at a high level, but detailed planning and execution often require a more refined and agreed-upon scope. This option implies that scope approval is a prerequisite to engaging the team in detailed planning, which can delay the process if not handled efficiently. However, in a hybrid approach, planning is more iterative, so scope and details evolve as the project progresses, which makes Option D more accurate in this context.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a project and the first task is to assist in creating the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). Which tool, technique or document is used as starting point for an effective WBS creation? *

o.t: Scope baseline
Activity list
Project charter
WBS dictionary

questions.e: Option C. Project charter refers to a document that formally authorizes the project and provides high-level information such as the project's objectives, key stakeholders, and overall scope. While the project charter is crucial for initiating the project, it does not contain the detailed scope information required to create an effective Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). The project charter provides the overall direction for the project, but the creation of the WBS requires a more detailed understanding of the project's scope, which is found in the scope baseline. Therefore, the project charter is not the best starting point for WBS creation; instead, the scope baseline is more appropriate for this purpose.

questions.q: A project manager is in a successful automotive company with high quality standards. The project manager needs to ensure that they create a high-quality WBS. Which of the following is not a key characteristic of a high quality WBS? *

o.t: Deliverable oriented
Hierarchical
The 100% rule
Customer focused

questions.e: The correct answer is D. Customer focused. While customer focus is important in project management overall, it is not a key characteristic of a high-quality Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). A WBS is designed to be deliverable oriented (A), hierarchical (B), and adheres to the 100% rule (C)—which ensures that the WBS captures all the work needed to complete the project. Customer focus pertains more to broader project outcomes rather than the specific structure of a WBS.

questions.q: A company initiated a project to build a new hydropower plant. Analysis was performed to determine regulatory, safety, and security compliance requirements. After the analysis, it was apparent that some elements necessary to achieve compliance may be difficult and expensive to implement. Stakeholders are concerned about the added cost and complexity and have differing opinions on the importance of compliance and its potential implications. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the stakeholders and emphasize the importance of compliance and the costs of non-compliance.
Review the stakeholder register and determine which stakeholders have the highest authority and influence.
Escalate the compliance concerns and the disparity between stakeholder opinions to the project sponsor.
Identify compliance requirements that can be excluded in order to align with stakeholder expectations.

questions.e: The correct answer is A. Meet with the stakeholders and emphasize the importance of compliance and the costs of non-compliance. In projects with regulatory, safety, and security compliance requirements, it is crucial for the project manager to ensure that stakeholders understand the importance of compliance. Non-compliance can lead to severe consequences, including legal penalties, safety risks, and reputational damage. Meeting with stakeholders to discuss these implications and addressing their concerns is the best approach to align their understanding with the project's obligations.

questions.q: Which of the following project artifacts do not utilize the WBS as an input? *

o.t: Project schedule
Project scope
Risk management plan
Quality plan

questions.e: The correct answer is B. Project scope. The project scope defines the work that needs to be accomplished and serves as an input for creating the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), not the other way around. The WBS is derived from the project scope, and it breaks down the scope into smaller, more manageable components. Therefore, the project scope is not an artifact that directly utilizes the WBS as an input; rather, the WBS is created based on the scope. In contrast, the project schedule, risk management plan, and quality plan all utilize the WBS as an input to guide planning and ensure that all work is accounted for.

questions.q: During acceptance testing of a deliverable, some senior stakeholders complain that a feature essential to their department was not included. What should the project manager have done to prevent this? *

o.t: Consulted lessons learned from similar projects to adapt processes
Prepared a change management plan and logged changes during project implementation
Analyzed the project charter and developed a scope management plan
Prepared a prototype and conducted a product demo with stakeholders

questions.e: Option C. Analyzed the project charter and developed a scope management plan refers to activities related to defining and managing the project's scope. Analyzing the project charter involves reviewing the initial high-level objectives and scope defined at the start of the project. This helps in understanding the project's overall goals but does not directly address stakeholder needs throughout the project. Developing a scope management plan involves outlining how the project's scope will be defined, validated, and controlled. While this is crucial for managing scope changes and ensuring alignment with project goals, it does not directly address the proactive engagement of stakeholders. In this context, analyzing the project charter and developing a scope management plan are foundational activities. However, they are not as effective in preventing issues related to missing features as actively involving stakeholders through prototypes and demos. Prototypes and demos help ensure that stakeholder requirements are met and provide opportunities for early feedback, which is key to preventing such complaints during acceptance testing.

questions.q: A transportation company is transforming its operational processes and the main system this company uses to move freight. The scope statement is in place. An iterative delivery approach has been agreed by all stakeholders. What does the project manager need to do next to help the team understand the work that needs to be done? *

o.t: Start working on the project management plan with work packages, a detailed schedule, and work assignments for team members.
Work directly with stakeholders on the work breakdown structure (WBS) and assign tasks with a required timeline for each team member to start the work.
Work with the team to decompose the scope into a WBS and work packages in order to create required deliverables and timelines.
Create the requirements management plan to outline how project requirements will be collected, analyzed, and documented, and then assign requirements to team members.

questions.e: The correct answer is C. Work with the team to decompose the scope into a WBS and work packages in order to create required deliverables and timelines. In an iterative delivery approach, it's essential to break down the scope into manageable components. This involves creating a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) to decompose the overall scope into smaller, more manageable work packages. This helps the team understand the specific tasks and deliverables required, and allows for the development of detailed timelines and assignments for each work package.

questions.q: A project integrates with several systems developed by various vendors and one of these vendors has gone out of business. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Meet with this vendor to identify a replacement.
Review the risk register and update the issue log.
Calculate the delay and notify the project sponsor of the new timeline.
Negotiate with another vendor to produce the deliverable.

questions.e: The correct answer is B. Review the risk register and update the issue log. When a vendor goes out of business, it represents a significant issue that needs to be managed. The first step is to review the risk register to identify if this scenario was anticipated and to understand any mitigation strategies that were planned. Updating the issue log will document the problem and trigger the process of resolving it. This step is crucial for understanding the impact, communicating with stakeholders, and planning the next steps to address the issue, such as finding a replacement vendor or revising the project plan.

questions.q: An events company is planning a new event for a client that holds biannual conferences. The project is being managed by a new project manager who has reviewed the lessons learned log from the last event and is concerned that a past issue may reoccur. How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Identify the root cause and consult with stakeholders.
Handle the issue if it arises during the event planning.
Recommend rescheduling the upcoming conference.
Implement the same strategies used in the last event.

questions.e: The correct answer is A. Identify the root cause and consult with stakeholders. Before taking action, it's essential for the project manager to understand the root cause of the past issue that may recur. Consulting with stakeholders helps to gain insights into the problem and its impact, and allows for a more informed approach to prevent the issue from recurring. Identifying and addressing the root cause proactively can help implement effective strategies and solutions to avoid similar problems in the upcoming event.

questions.q: A project manager is working on the development of a business case to secure funding and resources. What is needed to ensure that the right priority is assigned to the project? *

o.t: Developing the most efficient delivery plan
Developing a clear and detailed project schedule
Aligning the project with company’s goals and objectives
Aligning the project with company’s roadmap

questions.e: The correct answer is C. Aligning the project with company’s goals and objectives. To ensure the right priority is assigned to the project, it is crucial to align the project with the company’s goals and objectives. This alignment ensures that the project contributes to the strategic direction of the organization and demonstrates its value and importance, which is essential for securing funding and resources. While a clear project schedule and an efficient delivery plan are important, they are secondary to ensuring that the project supports the overall goals and objectives of the company.

questions.q: The change control board (CCB) has evaluated and approved several change requests in a timely manner in the last several weeks. However, implementation of the changes is taking more time than anticipated. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Revise the change control system to allow only critical changes to be raised.
Acquire additional resources to ensure the project milestones are met.
Perform a detailed risk analysis to determine the impact of the time required to implement the changes on the success of the project.
Monitor implementation of the changes to ensure that change management procedures are being followed.

questions.e: The correct answer is D. Monitor implementation of the changes to ensure that change management procedures are being followed. If the implementation of approved changes is taking more time than anticipated, the project manager should ensure that the change management procedures are being followed correctly. Monitoring the implementation process helps to identify any issues or bottlenecks and ensures that changes are being executed as planned. This approach helps to maintain control over the change process and addresses any delays or challenges in a timely manner.

questions.q: A project team's performance has declined for the last three iterations. Some of the team members are disappointed, and raise their concerns during the retrospective meeting. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Identify potential failure points based on the iteration workload.
Motivate the team to perform better.
Focus on remediation, not merely on correcting symptoms.
Compare the team's performance against other project teams.

questions.e: The correct answer is C. Focus on remediation, not merely on correcting symptoms. When a project's team performance declines and concerns are raised, it's important for the project manager to address the root causes rather than just the symptoms. Focusing on remediation involves identifying underlying issues affecting performance and implementing solutions to address these root causes. This approach helps to resolve the core problems and improve overall team performance sustainably.

questions.q: A project manager learns that the project team will miss a milestone because team member A has not completed the task requirements needed by team member B. When meeting with team member A, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Direct team member A to turn over the responsibilities for completing the task requirements to team member B.
Identify any obstacles to meeting the task requirements and determine if team member A needs help completing them.
Ask team member A to work directly with team member B to complete the requirements in order to meet the milestone.
Ask team member A to recommend a replacement who can complete the task requirements.

questions.e: The correct answer is B. Identify any obstacles to meeting the task requirements and determine if team member A needs help completing them. When a project team member's delay is impacting a milestone, the project manager should first understand the reasons behind the delay. This involves identifying any obstacles or challenges that team member A might be facing and assessing whether they need additional support or resources to complete their task. This approach addresses the root cause of the issue and helps facilitate the completion of the requirements in a constructive manner.

questions.q: During a hybrid project, a project manager reviews the project team's performance and realizes that the team's velocity is not fast enough to meet the next review gate goal. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Prioritize the contents of the backlog and remove some stories.
Increase the sprint duration to allow the team more time.
Use the standup meeting to assess impediments and problems.
Create a change request to modify the review gate goals.

questions.e: The correct answer is C. Use the standup meeting to assess impediments and problems. In a hybrid project, where Agile practices are incorporated, using daily standup meetings to identify and address impediments is crucial for improving team velocity. This approach allows the project manager to uncover and resolve issues that may be affecting the team’s performance. By focusing on impediments and problems, the project manager can help the team overcome obstacles and improve their velocity, which is essential for meeting review gate goals.

questions.q: A project leader is on a very complex project, which is in the middle of a sprint. A stakeholder comes across the project manager and informed them about a requirement and proposed to call a meeting to inform team members. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Call a meeting with the stakeholder and a team member
Ask the stakeholder to come to the war room and explain the requirement to the team
Call a meeting with the stakeholder an all team members
Add to the product backlog to be treated in next iteration

questions.e: The correct answer is D. Add to the product backlog to be treated in the next iteration. In Agile practices, changes to requirements or new information are typically handled through the product backlog. During an ongoing sprint, the team should focus on the work committed to for that sprint. Any new requirements or changes should be added to the product backlog, where they can be prioritized and planned for the next iteration or sprint. This ensures that the current sprint remains focused and prevents disruption to the ongoing work.

questions.q: As part of a temporary assignment, a project manager is leading a business project. During a daily status meeting, it was discovered that the development team had not completed a critical task. This issue is delaying the current iteration. The ability to take the actions needed to address this issue is beyond the authority of the project team. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Delay the current iteration and inform the stakeholders of the issue.
Invite the project team to a swarming session to define a solution.
Adjust the project timeline to accommodate the development delay.
Escalate the issue to the project sponsor to define the next steps.

questions.e: The correct answer is D. Escalate the issue to the project sponsor to define the next steps. If the issue is beyond the authority of the project team and is affecting the project, it is important to escalate the problem to the project sponsor or other higher-level stakeholders. The project sponsor has the authority to make decisions, allocate resources, or take actions necessary to resolve the issue and mitigate its impact on the project. Escalating the issue ensures that it is addressed appropriately and that necessary support or decisions are made to keep the project on track.

questions.q: In a program, several groups are identifying problem solving techniques and each group presents a proposal. Among those listed, which is valid? *

o.t: Performing project health checks
Reading literature related to your industry
Establishing a project suggestion box
All of the above

questions.e: The correct answer is D. All of the above. All the listed options are valid problem-solving techniques that can be applied in different contexts within a program: Performing project health checks helps identify issues and areas for improvement by assessing the current status of projects. Reading literature related to your industry provides valuable insights and best practices that can inform problem-solving approaches. Establishing a project suggestion box allows team members to contribute ideas and solutions, fostering a collaborative problem-solving environment. Each of these methods can contribute to effective problem-solving in a program.

questions.q: An organization decides to implement the Scrum delivery framework. The project manager is using an impediment board with the Scrum team to identify and raise impediments. What should happen after the impediments are recorded? *

o.t: Address the highest priority impediments from the log and ensure that it is removed so that the team can continue to reach the sprint’s objective.
Prioritize impediments based on their levels of importance and in relation to those that are already on the log.
Publish and post the impediments log and make it visible to everyone.
Communicate that the impediment is removed to the involved parties and update the impediments log.

questions.e: Option B. Prioritize impediments based on their levels of importance and in relation to those that are already on the log focuses on the process of managing and addressing impediments. Explanation: Prioritization: This involves assessing each impediment based on its impact on the project and the team. Not all impediments are equal; some may have a more significant effect on the team's ability to meet sprint goals or deliverables. By prioritizing impediments, you can ensure that the most critical issues are addressed first. In Relation to Existing Impediments: Impediments should be evaluated not just in isolation but also in the context of other recorded issues. This helps to manage and address them in a sequence that optimally resolves the most pressing issues and avoids creating new bottlenecks. In Practice: While prioritizing impediments is important, the actual resolution of these issues takes precedence. Prioritization ensures that you focus on the most critical impediments, but the primary goal should be to address and remove these impediments to ensure the team can continue progressing effectively. Thus, option A, which involves actively addressing and removing high-priority impediments, is more directly aligned with the Scrum framework’s focus on continuous improvement and overcoming obstacles.

questions.q: A project has the following characteristics: · The project manager is being asked to deliver a business result in a compressed timeline; the original timeline was one month, but the new requested timeline is two weeks. · In the resource planning activity, the project manager heard from another team member that no technical resources are available to join the team; however, the project manager knows the technical resource manager from a previous project. What is the first action the project manager should take? *

o.t: Ensure the product owner knows that there is an issue with acquiring a technical resource.
Escalate the technical resource issue to upper management.
Verify the availability of resources by meeting with the previously known technical resource manager.
Contact a third-party vendor to obtain a technical resource.

questions.e: The correct answer is C. Verify the availability of resources by meeting with the previously known technical resource manager. The first action should be to verify the availability of resources with the technical resource manager, whom the project manager knows from a previous project. This approach allows the project manager to directly check the availability of the needed resources and potentially resolve the issue before escalating it to upper management or seeking external vendors.
